Results: A total of 60,922 mosquitoes belonging to eight genera (Culex, Anopheles, Aedes, Armigeres, Malaya, Mansonia, Tripteroides, and Toxorhynchites) were identified. Of these, 16,044 were female Cx. quinquefasciatus. Gravid traps showed higher relative trapping efficiency of female Cx. quinquefasciatus than light traps, with the highest efficiency observed in Jhapa (3.60:1). Temporal trends varied across locations; however, overall Cx. quinquefasciatus abundance peaked during the spring and summer months (March-May), coinciding with the monsoon period, and was positively correlated with climatic factors. W. bancrofti infection rates varied by location and trap type, with gravid traps yielding higher infection rates, particularly in Jhapa. A total of 785 pools of Cx. quinquefasciatus were screened. Pool positivity and infection prevalence (MLE) ranged from 10.3% to 17.6% and 0.5% to 0.9% in Dhading, 12.5% to 36.8% and 0.9% to 2.0% in Jhapa, and 5.3% to 20.0% and 0.3% to 1.5% in Kapilvastu, respectively. Conclusions: The study highlights ongoing transmission in three LF-endemic areas of Nepal, emphasising the need for continued surveillance in high-risk areas and periods. Gravid trap-based xenomonitoring could complement community-based W. bancrofti surveillance by identifying hotspots and optimising the timing and targeting of LF elimination interventions.
na79dbfdf52ba: Introduction McCune-Albright syndrome (MAS) is a rare congenital disorder affecting endocrine, skeletal and dermatological systems. MAS is often coded as fibrous dysplasia (FD) in routine health data, which includes other conditions and does not allow precise identification. This coding gap complicates reliable epidemiological estimates and clinical characterization. The study MAScINSIGHT aims to address this by investigating MAS features within FD-coded cohorts. Methods and analysis MAScINSIGHT is a retrospective observational study using a federated network of data in the OMOP Common Data Model. Routine data from multiple sites will be analyzed within a federated setting to assess endocrine abnormalities and treatment patterns in patients with FD or MAS. Ethics and dissemination Analyses will be performed locally at the data partner, with only aggregate statistics made available and centrally analyzed. The study protocol was approved by the ethics committee (reference number: 2026-18760-retrospektiv). Findings will be disseminated through open-access publications and patient-oriented reports.
n8b0669d5f151: Background/Objectives: Maternal Autoantibody-Related Autism (MARA) is a recently defined subset of autism characterized by specific combinations of maternal autoantibodies which cross the placenta and bind neurodevelopmentally critical target proteins. A clinical multi-ELISA MARA assay was recently rigorously analytically validated. The primary objective of this study was to assess the potential performance of this MARA autoantibody assay for predicting autism risk in high-risk populations. Secondary objectives were to establish the significant MARA autoantibody combinations and verify clinical discrimination in an external cohort. Methods: Bio-banked plasma samples from mothers of 420 autism and 335 typically developing (TD) children were analyzed by ELISA for MARA autoantibodies in combination. Transcendent autoantibody pairwise combinations were identified in discovery where both autoantibodies in a combination exceeded the values of every control participant. Permutation testing was used to establish that the probability of observed results significantly exceeded chance. Performance was then validated in an independent cohort (mothers of 42 autistic and 90 TD children). Results: Transcendent antibody levels were discovered in 70 mothers (16.7% of autism cases; no typically developing participants) in the discovery cohort. Specificity and positive predictive values for autism were 100% by construct. An external cohort showed similar performance with 14 (33.3%) transcendents. Permutation testing of each cohort demonstrated probabilities of transcendent cases to be significantly higher than expected be chance. Conclusions: The data reported here provides evidence for a high-risk subset of mothers of children with autism identified by the MARA autoantibody assay which enables further clinical validation.
n31d17ad462a1: Background: Early-onset neonatal sepsis (EONS) remains a major cause of neonatal morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries. Maternal vaginal pathogenic bacterial colonization and HIV infection may increase the risk of EONS through vertical transmission and immune dysregulation, but prospective evidence from sub-Saharan Africa is limited. This study assessed the association between maternal HIV status, vaginal pathogenic bacterial colonization, and EONS among women delivering at five selected health facilities in Mwanza City, Tanzania. Methods: A prospective comparative cohort study was conducted between August 2023 and February 2025 among 580 pregnant women delivering at five selected health facilities in Mwanza City. A maternal lower vaginal swab was collected before delivery for bacterial culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Neonates were followed for seven days after birth to identify EONS using standardized clinical and laboratory criteria, with culture confirmation where applicable. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox proportional hazards regression were used to estimate incidence rates and identify independent predictors of neonatal sepsis. Results: Overall, 89 neonates developed EONS, yielding a cumulative incidence of 15.3% and an incidence rate of 2.42 per 100 person-days (95% CI: 1.97-2.98). Twenty-four (27.0%) cases were culture-confirmed, while 65 (73.0%) were clinically diagnosed. Neonates born to colonized mothers had substantially higher sepsis incidence than those born to non-colonized mothers (3.41 vs. 0.34 per 100 person-days). After adjustment, maternal vaginal bacterial colonization was the strongest predictor of neonatal sepsis (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 9.52, 95% CI: 3.47-26.09; p<0.001). Maternal HIV infection independently increased the hazard of neonatal sepsis by 76% (aHR 1.76, 95% CI: 1.14-2.73; p=0.011), while maternal malaria doubled the risk (aHR 2.74, 95% CI: 1.43-5.22; p=0.002). Escherichia coli (E. coli) accounted for 58.3% of culture-confirmed neonatal infections, followed by both Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus (20.8% each). Conclusion: Maternal vaginal pathogenic bacterial colonization was strongly associated with early-onset neonatal sepsis. Maternal HIV infection and malaria were also independently associated with increased sepsis. The findings support strengthening maternal infection prevention, neonatal surveillance, and microbiological diagnostic capacity, while prospective intervention studies are needed to determine whether targeted screening and prevention of maternal bacterial colonization can reduce neonatal sepsis.
n7e2fa296f426: Background. Suppressed fibrinolysis (fibrinolysis resistance) is increasingly recognised as a driver of organ failure in sepsis, yet trials in sepsis-induced coagulopathy have largely targeted coagulation rather than fibrinolysis. This study combined an observational ICU cohort with nested analyses of plasma fibrinolysis proteins and ex vivo reversibility, modelling the potential mortality reduction from restoring fibrinolytic capacity to inform trial design. Methods. In 188 adults admitted to ICU with sepsis, repeated tissue plasminogen activator (tPA)-enhanced viscoelastometric testing quantified fibrinolysis resistance as the fibrin adjusted lysis time (TPA-LT/FIBA10) and as ordinal Grades 1-3 of worsening resistance. Adjusted logistic regression and time-varying Cox models related fibrinolysis resistance to death within 28 days of admission, with unmeasured confounding assessed by E-values. In nested sub-studies, plasma fibrinolysis proteins were measured and whole blood was tested ex vivo for reversal of resistance by supplemental tPA, plasminogen, or an inhibitory antibody to a2-antiplasmin (a2AP iAb). Ex vivo effects were modelled onto the observed fibrinolysis resistance-mortality relationship using a hypothetical intervention distribution framework. Results. Each e-fold (~2.72) increase in TPA-LT/FIBA10 was associated with a 2.2-fold (95% CI 1.5-3.3) increase in the odds of death in the fully adjusted logistic model and a 2.3-fold (1.6-3.2) increased hazard in the time-varying Cox model. Comparing the least (Grade 1) with the worst (Grade 3) resistance state, the odds ratio was 7.4 (2.4-23) and the hazard ratio 6.7 (3.0-15). Associations were robust to unmeasured confounding, with E-values of 3-13. Grade 3 resistance showed the highest PAI-1/tPA and a2AP/plasminogen ratios. Ex vivo supplementation with plasminogen or a2AP iAb reversed fibrinolysis resistance from Grade 3 to Grade 1. Modelling these effects yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of 18-21% across Grades 2 and 3, and 32-36% in Grade 3. Conclusions. Fibrinolysis resistance measured at the bedside in sepsis reflects mechanistically reversible changes in fibrinolytic balance ex vivo. Modelling reversal by plasminogen supplementation or a2AP inhibition yielded hypothetical absolute mortality reductions of up to 32% in the most severe resistance state. These hypothesis-generating estimates identify candidate interventions and provide a rationale for a clinical trial.
n2a57ec561c11: Purpose: High resolution arterial spin labeling (ASL)-based perfusion imaging is desirable for many applications but suffers from low SNR and motion sensitivity due to the necessity for highly segmented readouts. Acquisition and reconstruction strategies were optimized for motion-robust high-resolution pseudo-continuous arterial spin labeling (pCASL) of the brain at 3T using segmented 3D Gradient and Spin Echo (3D-GRASE) at 2.0-mm isotropic resolution. Methods: A high-resolution 3D-GRASE pCASL sequence was implemented at 3T and evaluated with a focus on the interaction between background suppression strength and motion-corrected reconstruction, together with the fat suppression and control-tag subtraction strategies that strong suppression requires. Motion correction was performed using a novel motion-compensated (alignedSENSE-based) reconstruction that simultaneously estimates the motion and image, accounting for contrast changes between tag and control data. Eight healthy volunteers were scanned under motion-free and cued motion conditions. Image quality was assessed against motion-free reference images using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and a structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Results: The optimized acquisition-reconstruction pipeline enabled robust 2.0-mm isotropic pCASL at 3T and showed improved resistance to motion-related degradation. Strong BGS provided near-complete suppression of static tissue, and water excitation reduced lipid contamination and improved coil sensitivity estimation. The regularized alignedSENSE motion correction further improved perfusion-image quality, increasing SSIM by 18.7% under Strong BGS. Conclusion: Robust high-resolution pCASL at 3T can be achieved through combined optimization of acquisition and reconstruction. The combination of Strong BGS, water excitation, reference-superimposed processing, and regularized motion correction mitigates motion-related degradation and yields higher-quality perfusion images for high-resolution ASL.
nbfd413417b01: Objective and design: To test whether the hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF1A) axis links transcriptional, cellular, biomarker and host-genetic features of severe COVID-19, in a retrospective multi-scale observational study of public cohorts and one hospital cohort. Material or subjects: 35,268 hospitalized patients (Mexican national registry); 1,100 samples from five bulk RNA-seq cohorts; 25,773 peripheral neutrophils from six individuals; 326 hospitalized patients (Sao Paulo, Brazil); 93 hospitalized patients (University Clinical Center Kragujevac, Serbia). Treatment: None. Methods: Within-cohort effect sizes for a 10-gene HIF1A panel; single-cell pathway scoring; logistic regression and gradient boosting with SHAP; TaqMan genotyping of HIF1A rs11549465 and rs41508050; cross-validation with bootstrap confidence intervals. Results: HIF1A (mean Cohen d +0.39) and LDHA (+0.76) were higher in severe disease in all five cohorts. Neutrophils of all three patients who failed extubation scored higher than those of both weaned patients and over-expressed S100A8/A9. C-reactive protein dominated ICU prediction; laboratory variables raised the AUC from 0.636 to 0.794. In Kragujevac, a clinical model predicted severe outcome (AUC 0.84, 95% CI 0.75 to 0.92). rs11549465 CT/TT carriers had lower mortality (1/11 vs 28/78; p = 0.095). Conclusions: HIF1A pathway activation is reproducible across cohorts and localizes to an alarmin-rich neutrophil state; host-genetic effects require larger cohorts.
ne303321b8e5f: Adolescent psychotic-like experiences, particularly those that are distressing and persistent (dpPLEs), may elevate risk for a range of psychiatric disorders, yet the relative predictive contributions of brain structure, genetics, and environment to dpPLEs remain unknown. Using four timepoints from 7,399 children in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, we developed stacked ensemble machine-learning models integrating cortical morphometry and whole-brain microstructural properties, polygenic risk scores, family psychiatric history, and childhood environmental factors to predict adolescent dpPLEs. Environmental predictors alone, driven by area deprivation index, neighborhood drug-related crime, and cumulative early adversity, were the strongest predictive domain (ROC-AUC = 0.687 {+/-} 0.003), outperforming genetic (0.619 {+/-} 0.020) and all imaging models (0.588-0.650). Adding genetic risk to environmental features produced the best-performing model overall (ROC-AUC = 0.697 {+/-} 0.007), whereas adding neuroimaging yielded no further incremental gain (ROC-AUC=0.683-0.696). Beyond environmental exposures, family history of psychosis, cross-disorder polygenic risk, and both globally distributed and regionally specific imaging components contributed to prediction. Childhood environmental factors thus capture a core predictive signal preceding dpPLEs, while genetic and neuroimaging features added comparatively modest discriminative prediction value, but may offer complementary biological insights.
nc52cb2788ecc: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is associated with systemic immune dysregulation, but the specific immune cell populations and activation states contributing to disorder susceptibility remain poorly understood. Identifying these dynamic immune mechanisms may help uncover new opportunities for immune-targeted interventions in depression. We combined single-cell transcriptomic data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) under resting and stimulated conditions with population genetic analyses to identify immune-cell populations and activation states linked to MDD susceptibility. Psoriasis was included as a comparator phenotype where ground truth regarding immune involvement is established. We identified immune-cell programmes enriched for disease-associated genetic risk and used Mendelian randomisation to prioritise genes potentially contributing to disease susceptibility. We find that psoriasis heritability predominantly localised to activated lymphocyte populations following CD3/CD28 stimulation, consistent with its established adaptive immune pathology. In contrast, MDD heritability was enriched within natural killer (NK) cell populations among resting and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated PBMCs. Genetic analyses further prioritised NK-cell-associated genes, including CCL5, GZMA and SYNE2, with evidence of genetically predicted effects on MDD risk. By connecting genetic evidence for immune involvement in depression with specific cellular and functional contexts, our findings implicate NK-cell transcriptional programmes in MDD susceptibility, highlighting NK-cell immune signalling as a potential target for immunomodulatory treatment strategies.
n4d6fe529595e: Background. Despite advances in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis, RSV remains a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in infants. Immunity at the site of infection is potentially important yet airway mucosal immunity against RSV infection remains poorly defined. Methods. We collected nasal and blood samples across three pediatric cohorts: 1) children presenting to the emergency department with respiratory symptoms; 2) infants and mothers presenting to an urban hospital system across the RSV season; 3) infants born to mothers vaccinated with maternal pre-Fusion (F) vaccine. We analyzed mucosal and serologic anti-RSV antibodies and assessed for factors impacting titer magnitude and durability. Results. Specimens from 285 infants/young children and 39 mothers were analyzed. Mucosal anti-RSV antibody levels were lower in infants presenting with RSV infection compared to age-matched controls both in infants experiencing their first viral season (p = 0.0011) and older children (p < 0.0001). Higher levels of mucosal antibodies were seen in infants whose mothers received maternal pre-F vaccination, with IgG against RSV fusion protein tightly correlating between infant serum and nasal compartments (p < 0.0001). However, mucosal anti-RSV IgG waned significantly by 6 months of age (p < 0.0001). Conclusions. Higher mucosal anti-RSV antibody levels are associated with protection against RSV-related illness. Current immunoprophylactic strategies drive robust anti-RSV IgG responses in the infant mucosal and serological compartments; however, passive immunity wanes over 6 months. These results suggest that RSV immunization strategies optimizing durable mucosal immunity may protect infants from RSV-related respiratory illness.
nf385ce6a5ed7: Objectives: To assess whether local artificial intelligence updates for diabetic retinopathy screening that improve image-level probabilities also improve patient-level detection, flagging and net benefit. Methods: This retrospective evaluation used four systems, BRSET source data and two external cohorts, mBRSET and DeepDRiD, with separate audit and evaluation patients. Updates were fitted and selected on audits of 25-200 patients; probability recalibration and operating policies were selected separately. Outcomes included Brier loss, patient detection, flags and net benefit at four threshold probabilities (p=0.05-0.30). Comparators were no update, flag all and flag none. Conditional patient-cluster intervals compared updates with no update; simple-policy comparisons were descriptive. Results: At audit budget 200, mean Brier loss improved in all eight cohort-system comparisons. In mBRSET, flags rose from 154-442 to 809-951 per 1,000 patients and missed positives fell from 51-133 to 2-14 (5.69-9.48 additional flags per additional detection). In mBRSET at p=0.05, three of four updates had lower mean net benefit than flag all; at p=0.20, all four exceeded flag all but remained below no update. In DeepDRiD at p=0.20, the APTOS update increased mean net benefit by 0.0510 over no update and exceeded both simple policies. Discussion: Image-level improvement did not ensure patient-level benefit. Flag increases were consistent with image-level targets applied to patients with about four images. Conclusion: Local updates should be judged on patient-level detection, flags and net benefit against unchanged, flag-all and flag-none policies, not on image-level metrics alone.
n723a02bbc666: Polygenic scores for major depression, schizophrenia and bipolar disorder have been related to treatment outcome. We analysed 4,007 patients of European ancestry from 7 cohorts: three with major depression (STAR*D, GSRD, PANDORA), two with bipolar disorder (STEP-BD, Barcelona) and two with schizophrenia (CATIE, HSRRm). The three scores were computed with PRS-CS from the latest Psychiatric Genomics Consortium studies. The primary outcome was good response or good course, harmonized from each cohort's instrument. Firth logistic regression within cohorts, adjusted for age, sex and ancestry components, was followed by random-effects pooling. A higher depression score was associated with lower odds of a good outcome (odds ratio per standard deviation 0.88, 95% confidence interval 0.79-0.99, p = .04; false discovery rate q = .11). The estimate remained below one in all 8 sensitivity analyses, including adjustment for baseline severity, and was negative in all 5 cohorts with a continuous improvement measure. The schizophrenia score pointed the same way (odds ratio 0.93, 95% confidence interval 0.85-1.01) with no heterogeneity. The bipolar score showed no pooled effect (odds ratio 0.97), and its direction differed by diagnosis. In pooled data spanning three diagnoses, higher polygenic liability to depression was nominally associated with a less favourable treatment outcome, although the association did not survive correction for multiple testing; schizophrenia liability showed a similar directional trend. These findings support further evaluation of disorder liability in multivariable models of treatment outcome.
naf6a12b1b23a: Longitudinal causal effect estimation is complicated by time-varying confounding and treatment-confounder feedback loops. Existing methods generally require data-specific nuisance-model fitting, and many are tailored to prespecified treatment sequences or prediction horizons, leading to time-consuming computation at deployment. We introduce *Policy In-Context Longitudinal causal Effect estimation with Prior-data Fitted Networks* (**PICLE-PFN**), the first foundation model for longitudinal causal effect estimation that supports *dynamic* treatment policies. PICLE-PFN represents target policies through in-context history-decision demonstrations, providing a unified interface for a broad class of treatment policies. Pretrained over synthetic data sampled from longitudinal structural causal models, PICLE-PFN amortizes causal effect estimation across datasets, policies, and horizons. Given a new observational dataset and target policy, it directly predicts conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) in one forward pass without task-specific training or hyperparameter tuning. Across synthetic and semi-synthetic longitudinal benchmarks, PICLE-PFN achieves competitive RMSE and substantially improved uncertainty calibration with a fraction of deployment runtime, compared to state-of-the-art conventional estimators trained and tuned separately for each dataset.
nae8fe6a96cac: Physics-constrained machine learning (PCML) integrates domain knowledge, first-principles, and physical constraints into AI/ML models. In this work, we present a step-by-step tutorial of a modular PCML framework, KKT-HardNet, and illustrate how it could be used for hybrid modeling, process simulation, optimization and model predictive control in a single platform. KKT-HardNet combines fast inference capabilities of neural networks with guaranteed satisfaction of algebraic constraints through differential projection. It can handle heterogeneous data and enforce both linear and nonlinear equality and inequality constraints. The modular design supports custom neural-network backbones and user-defined projection mechanisms for PCML. To enable efficient end-to-end training, KKT-HardNet exploits implicit function theorem to backpropagate through the projection layer. This avoids computationally expensive automatic differentiation. This work also introduces an exact reduced-order Fischer-Burmeister reformulation and a primal-dual interior-point method as an alternative projection solve strategy. We also provide a diverse set of benchmarking problems for PCML in engineering applications. KKT-HardNet achieves orders of magnitude better performance in terms of both constraint satisfaction and inference time. The KKT-HardNet code and the benchmark datasets are available at https://github.com/souls-tamu/kkt-hardnet .
n4355348078e4: Modern language models rely on subwording tokenization to define the discrete units of input processing, typically using methods like Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) that treat whitespace as a fixed semantic boundary. This design is inherently limited, as many meaningful concepts---including multiword expressions and the structured environments of formal languages like LaTeX---frequently span across whitespaces. While recent superword tokenization methods attempt to address this by relaxing whitespace constraints, they often rely on greedy frequency-driven merging that fails to account for token length or the specific needs of underrepresented domain-specific languages. In this paper, we introduce Adaptive Frequency Threshold Byte Pair Encoding (AdaBPE), a new tokenization method that leverages an adaptive frequent-pattern mining approach. AdaBPE features a twofold dynamicity: it adapts minimum frequency thresholds based on both the length of a candidate token, to prevent favoring frequent short patterns, and its type, to distinguish between general and formal language patterns, using LaTeX as case in point. This allows the model to efficiently allocate vocabulary capacity to domain-specific notations, such as LaTeX, even when they represent a small fraction of the training data. We evaluate AdaBPE across five datasets spanning LaTeX and natural language, showing consistent gains in encoding efficiency and downstream language-model performance on domain-specific content without compromising general-language performance.
n7adfdb417515: Low-rank SVD-based compression offers a powerful strategy to reduce the computational costs of LLMs. However, existing methods face two key limitations: (i) global rank allocation, where uncalibrated error proxies fail to capture complex error propagation, and (ii) decomposition quality, where Fisher-based estimators suffer from severe rank collapse. In this work, we address these limitations by introducing Layer-wise Error Modeling Search (LEMS) and KFAC-SVD. LEMS advances rank allocation by introducing a layer-wise error surrogate that integrates local and global layer importance alongside a propagation bias, enabling effective global rank allocation via an ILP formulation. KFAC-SVD improves decomposition quality by utilizing token-wise statistics, mitigating the rank deficiency observed in prior Fisher-based SVD approaches. Across Mistral, Qwen3, and Llama 3 model families, we show that LEMS consistently outperforms existing search strategies, delivering significant zero-shot accuracy gains of up to 4.8 p.p. that generalize to model sizes of 70B parameters, while KFAC-SVD achieves an average perplexity improvement of 15%. Project page and code: https://lems-svd.github.io
n5125c811737b: Objective: To develop a unified vision-language model for prompt-conditioned quantitative ultrasound measurement that addresses the mismatch between continuous measurement targets and discrete token-based numerical prediction. Methods: This article presents HAD-VLM, a hybrid autoregressive-diffusion framework that combines autoregressive text generation with continuous measurement prediction within a shared backbone. Visual prompt tuning adapts the vision encoder to ultrasound images. A diffusion process predicts a five-component representation comprising caliper endpoint coordinates and measurement length. A post-processing strategy combining the proposed coordinate-length consistency mechanism with ensemble prediction is introduced to refine measurement estimates. We evaluate four echocardiographic measurement tasks on EchoNet-LVH, with additional assessments of medical question answering and X-ray vertebral measurement. Results: HAD-VLM achieves mean absolute errors of 1.36, 2.77, 3.05, and 1.16 mm for IVSd, LVIDd, LVIDs, and LVPWd, respectively, reducing errors by 21.4-37.6\% relative to the Vicuna-based autoregressive baseline. It also outperforms fine-tuned Qwen3-VL and direct MLP regression across all four tasks. Medical question answering performance is preserved on the evaluated dataset. For X-ray vertebral measurement, HAD-VLM reduces mean absolute error from 11.4 to 6.7 pixels. Conclusion: Integrating autoregressive language generation with diffusion-based continuous prediction improves quantitative medical image measurement while retaining prompt-conditioned task flexibility. Significance: HAD-VLM provides a unified approach to combining language interaction with anatomically grounded numerical prediction for quantitative medical image analysis.
n7480ee6eed25: Replay-based Continual Learning mitigates catastrophic forgetting by keeping a buffer of past samples, making buffer composition critical under a fixed memory budget. Recent coreset-based replay methods improve buffer quality using model-derived gradients, losses, or auxiliary optimization, but incur substantial computational overhead as memory is repeatedly updated. We propose CARES, a continual model-optimization-free approach for buffer construction that instead exploits the geometry of a frozen pretrained feature space using class-aware, density-weighted coverage. We evaluate CARES across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings. On Tiny-ImageNet, CARES is 2.3 to 8.8 times faster than existing coreset-based selectors. Although CARES achieves this speedup using no training signal from the continual learner, it ranks among the state of the art across balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy streams under online class- and task-incremental settings, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 7.58 percentage points under class imbalance while also attaining higher average accuracy on Tiny-ImageNet. Code will be released upon publication
nfb4f83395d87: While multimodal contrastive models like CLIP and CLAP successfully learn shared representations, their embeddings typically exhibit a persistent \emph{modality gap}. We propose addressing this separation through a purely geometric approach: changing the embedding domain from the unit sphere, $S^{d-1}$, to the probability simplex, $Δ^{d-1}$. Although both manifolds share the same intrinsic dimension, the simplex acts as a structural prior; its nonnegative, unit-mass constraints serve as a cross-modal calibration that forces both modalities to ground themselves in the same coordinate system. By attaching lightweight softmax adapters and using Total Variation similarity, we reduce the centroid $\ell_2$ gap by 97--99\% across five multimodal retrieval benchmarks. This confirms that simplicial geometry induces genuine semantic alignment, matching or exceeding the retrieval performance of standard unconstrained models.
n4245b70f3c2c: It is essential that we communicate with the entirety of an affected population during a crisis, including those who do not speak a region's dominant language(s). Commercial Translation tools offer a tempting solution to broaden access and can provide a lifeline when no other resources are available. However, Emergency response managers often operate in the dark regarding the quality and adequacy of these automated outputs. In this paper, we conduct a nationwide survey of emergency managers to understand their current workflows, perspectives, and operational challenges. We then evaluate commercial translation tools against these needs, shedding light on their utility and offering practical guidance on how and when these tools can be safely used in emergency response.
n4af4ead8c561: Collecting high-quality demonstrations remains a central bottleneck for learning dexterous manipulation. Teleoperation records executable robot actions, but it requires a complete robot setup and places the burden of coordinating many finger joints on the operator. Human demonstrations are easier to collect, but their motions must be estimated and retargeted to the robot, and they do not directly provide robot actions. In this paper, we introduce DexPort, a portable data-collection interface for high-DoF robot hands. It uses the same hand hardware for collection and deployment, avoiding a hand embodiment gap, and records both commanded joint targets and measured joint states. Our key observation is that a small set of skills can support a wide range of dexterous tasks. During collection, the operator moves the hand-held interface to specify the robot wrist motion and selects or adjusts skills that coordinate the finger motion. This removes the need to control each joint independently while retaining behaviors such as precise grasping and in-hand manipulation. We collect demonstrations across several real-world tasks and in unstructured environments without a robot arm. We then use behavior cloning to train visuomotor policies directly on the recorded wrist motions and hand commands, without skill labels. We evaluate across 4 tasks: pick-and-place with diverse objects, screwing with in-hand tool use, drawer stowage which requires simultaneous grasp and pulling, and a bimanual scanning task. We collect over 2,500 demonstrations with our portable device, in both laboratory and in-the-wild settings. Across our tasks, we see an improvement from 11% to 64% when using recorded robot commands instead of states, and an improvement from 36% to 78% for task success when using in-the-wild data.
nc7fea478b3ea: In LLM-agent opinion simulations, each agent reports the probability that a claim is true after seeing its own previous probability and the probabilities reported by its neighbors, and that number becomes its state in the next round. If the number describes the agent's position rather than the sentence it was shown, then rewriting the claim as its complement and replacing every probability p with 1 - p should return the complementary answer, so the two reports should sum to one. We test this with three small open models: Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.2-3B and Gemma-3-4B. On 2,304 agent states taken from a running network simulation, Qwen's paired reports sum to 1.18 on average, and on 48 real fact-checking claims from AVeriTeC they again exceed one. A controlled benchmark of 24 worlds, each with exactly two possible outcomes, shows the same failure in all three models. The discrepancy is two to ten times larger than the change produced by a same-meaning paraphrase, and it persists under repeated sampling and across peer group sizes and report strengths. When the reports are fed back into two populations that start from complementary states, the populations do not remain mirror images: their divergence is positive after five rounds for every model. Averaging each answer with the complement of its paired answer restores consistency by construction and lowers Brier loss averaged over the two wordings, but at the final round it beats the better of the two original wordings for only one of the three models. A schedule-by-targeting experiment on the same model gives a small, stable interaction because such sweeps keep the claim wording fixed. Consistency under rewording therefore needs its own test before simulated probabilities are read as beliefs
n8d55bb49e72e: Hospitals regularly buy software that clinicians and patients depend on. Because these purchases are costly, hard to reverse and can affect patient care, buyers look for evidence of which peer institutions already use a product and which systems it connects to. This evidence is public but scattered across vendor websites, press releases and third-party pages. Language-model agents can now collect it at low cost, but the correctness of the extracted claims is difficult to establish, and a wrongly listed customer can mislead buyers and misrepresent an organisation. We present a pipeline that builds a knowledge graph of customer and integration relations from the open web under one rule: every edge must be supported by a verbatim quote from its source page. Pages come from a deterministic crawl of each vendor's site and a budgeted ReAct agent that searches the rest of the web. A permissive extractor proposes relations with quotes, and a layered grounding stage decides which to keep, using a referent step that reads the whole page when a quote names only one side, deterministic checks, and a panel of five model calls voting on nine criteria. On 61 vendors, the pipeline reaches 0.94 precision and 0.71 recall against a page-level key covering the 6,428 candidate relations proposed by its extractor, whose verdicts were drafted by one model and re-checked with a second. Against the golden reference, the marketplace's own curated list, it scores lower, but 89% of the relations it keeps that the reference lacks are stated on a page. A confidence score built from the panel's votes keeps more correct relations than the fixed rule at the same precision, and reaches 0.90 precision at 0.90 recall. We also discuss how narrow, bounded model calls, string-matched evidence and voting address long-context degradation and run-to-run variance.
n3d87869a7de2: Few-shot industrial anomaly detection requires modeling category-specific normality from only a handful of defect-free images. Common approaches tie inference to stored exemplars, impose rigid linear structure, or risk reproducing anomalous content. Flownomaly instead casts the problem as normal-counterpart recovery in frozen DINOv2 feature space. Given normal supports, a velocity field is learned through conditional flow matching over frozen patch tokens to transport Gaussian noise toward normal features. Along straight paths, a single recovery step using one evaluation of the optimal field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without trajectory integration. The operating time governs how strongly recovery modifies a query token. With no anomalous validation samples available for tuning, a normal-only Jacobian gain-to-noise criterion selects this time from the supports alone. Squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts yield anomaly signals for both dense localization and image-level detection. Across 1-, 2-, and 4-shot benchmarks on MVTec-AD and VisA, together with sample-shot evaluations on Real-IAD, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance against recent category-specific methods. In the 1-shot setting, image- and pixel-level AUROC reach 97.8% and 98.0% on MVTec-AD and 95.3% and 98.7% on VisA, with a 2.1-point image-level AUROC improvement over the strongest baseline on VisA. Code is available at https://github.com/b-rbmp/Flownomaly.
n20aa2fb6ffaf: This paper proposes a five-level organization of message formation and understanding within thinking and activity in which ASI participates. Its central thesis is that a language model's context is fundamentally incapable of presenting the foundations of utterance formation for examination and verification. These foundations are established in advance by acquired schemas, systemic representations of the world of activity, and connections accepted as true within them. Neither context nor trained LLM weights, in themselves, attest to the presence of deliberately constructed systemic representations. The five levels distinguish systemic representations of the world of activity, a particular situation cut out from those representations, its narrative description, the full sense of a message, and text. A situation's schema-model is not identical to a story about it. A recipient reconstructs the full sense from an abbreviated text through jointly constructed and agreed-upon representations and joint activity. Reverse work proceeds from the full sense through an extended description and the situation's schema-model to the reconstruction of systemic foundations. The theoretical foundations draw on the systems methodology of G. P. Shchedrovitskiy, the structural differential of A. Korzybski, and the Meaning-Text theory of I. A. Mel'chuk. The contribution is a specific systemic-activity organization of content for examining and adjusting message foundations and controlling the consequences of their transformation. Further research concerns large graphical models of activity on reconstructible systemic foundations, distinct from text generation from context.
n9a6829979450: On-policy distillation aligns teacher feedback with a student's current behavior, yet acquiring useful supervision for multi-turn agents requires identifying both where guidance is needed and whether the student can sustain the interaction afterward. We introduce Frontier-OPD, which addresses this problem through the student's learning frontier: decision situations that remain challenging but admit useful autonomous continuation after brief teacher guidance. To operationalize this frontier, Frontier-OPD organizes on-policy experience into a shared-state trajectory graph, where trajectory-balanced aggregation of teacher-student disagreement identifies distinct intervention candidates while preserving the histories needed for replay. Short teacher bridges are then assessed by comparing agreement over the bridge and the ensuing student continuation with an equally long segment of the original trajectory, providing a behavioral proxy for guidance that the current student can build on. Accepted teacher responses augment ordinary distillation data, and fresh rollouts renew the frontier estimate as the policy changes. Experiments on ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld report higher mean autonomous performance than the compared distillation baselines across the evaluated student scales and teacher configurations, with ablations indicating complementary effects of candidate selection and guidance filtering. In one ALFWorld timing setting, the additional collection cost is offset by a shorter time to a target success rate.
n86683d31885c: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration. On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters. Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.
n41dc3e250194: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.
nf3e74da55903: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models perform well on robotic manipulation, yet remain brittle once their own actions carry them into states their training data barely covers. Recovering from such failures usually requires recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or a separate model at inference time. We introduce Backtrack, a lightweight failure detection and recovery mechanism for frozen VLAs that needs none of these. A small failure prediction head, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts of the frozen policy, reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate whether the current episode will fail. When the predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, retraces the arm's recently achieved motion, and hands control back to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier configuration. The head adds only 0.48-0.88% to the policy's parameter count. We evaluate Backtrack on LIBERO with three VLAs spanning two action-generation families: SmolVLA and $π$0.5, which use flow-matching action experts, and the autoregressive $π$0-FAST. On LIBERO-Long, the suite of long-horizon multi-step tasks and the one on which all three policies fail most often, Backtrack reduces each policy's failure rate by 19-48%, raising success by up to 7.4 percentage points; on the three shorter suites, where control success is already 85-99%, its effect is smaller. On MetaWorld, all twelve controller configurations tested with SmolVLA improve on the unassisted policy.
nfe02e1d22364: Fine-tuning on datasets of unknown origin can create a backdoor in the trained model when the data includes poisoned examples. Difficult to localise and remove, backdoors can persist through safety training. While parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods capture the full parameter changes introduced during training, they are not easily interpretable. We present the full method of TopKLoRA, extending the preliminary proposal of Masiak et al. (2025), an interpretable-by-design LoRA variant in which only the $k$ largest adapter latents are active at each token. Unlike SAEs, TopKLoRA is trained purely on downstream loss, where optimisation pressure incentivises learning functionally causal latents. We demonstrate this sparse LoRA adapter in a sleeper-agent backdoor case study where we create model organisms by fine-tuning gemma-2-2b, Qwen2.5-1.5B, and Qwen2.5-7B on a poisoned instruction-following dataset. For each organism, we identify and ablate a circuit that is both necessary and sufficient to implement the backdoor. Furthermore, our new fine-tuning method produces sparse circuits that are up to an order of magnitude smaller than a dense LoRA baseline, allowing surgical ablation of the malicious capability without sacrificing instruction-following performance. Finally, we propose a technique to construct model organisms with localised circuits using TopKLoRA latents and gradient-routing, which we use to validate the findings of our circuit search algorithm. We consider these findings as a step toward interpretable-by-design architectures that provide faithful units of analysis without compromising model performance. We share our code: https://github.com/interpretable-finetuning/TopKLoRA.
ne621649fd3cb: Latent communication requires both an effective continuous reasoning process and an interface through which an external model can leverage its intermediate computation. We present J-Comm, a framework comprising two core components. First, a training-free Geometric Agreement for Latent Reasoning (GEAR) reweights token candidates over existing model embeddings, which monotonically optimizes geometric consensus among candidate tokens in embedding space at each step. Second, we introduce an H+J (Hidden-and-Jacobian) communication interface that gives the Receiver two complementary views of the Sender's reasoning. The H channel supplies continuous inputs derived from feedback distributions, while the J channel conveys intermediate-state cues in vocabulary-indexed Jacobian-lens coordinates. Intuitively, H provides inputs for the Receiver to reason from, while J offers additional guidance within its computation. The Receiver reconstructs these cues using its own dictionary and injects them into intermediate layers during prefill, enabling communication without sharing key-value caches or requiring identical model widths. In Qwen3-8B to Qwen3-4B communication, J-Comm achieves the highest mean score across seven benchmarks, including 94.80% on MATH500, 54.55% on GPQA-Diamond, 73.33% on AIME2024+2025, and 62.93% success on ALFWorld. Compared with TextMAS, it improves performance by 1.29-8.59 percentage points and reduces generated text tokens by 19.2-74.8%.
ncbced115e63a: Generative recommendation with semantic IDs represents each item as a sequence of discrete codes derived from its semantic representation and predicts these codes to generate recommendations. Existing semantic-ID recommenders are typically trained with hard labels for the observed next item. Although such supervision identifies the target, it provides no explicit distributional information about alternative items conditioned on the same user history. Sequential recommenders can supply this item-level predictive knowledge, but transferring it to semantic-ID generation is challenging because the teacher and student operate in item and code spaces, respectively. We propose two complementary knowledge-distillation objectives for parallel semantic-ID recommenders, which predict all code positions simultaneously without autoregressive prefix conditioning. Item Distribution Matching (IDM) reconstructs a catalogue-level item distribution from the student's parallel code predictions and aligns it with the teacher's item distribution. Code Marginal Matching (CMM) projects the teacher's item probabilities onto each code position using fixed item-to-code assignments, then matches the resulting code marginals to the corresponding student heads. Both objectives transfer the teacher's soft distributional knowledge while preserving the student's parallel prediction structure. Experiments on benchmark datasets show that both methods consistently outperform existing state-of-the-art approaches. On average, IDM improves Recall@10 by 15.39%, while CMM improves NDCG@10 by 8.28%. These results demonstrate that distillation in either reconstructed item space or code-marginal space can substantially strengthen hard-label supervision for parallel generative recommendation.
n4296f6fb49b4: For agricultural advisory, generating an answer is only part of the problem: the system must also control unsafe requests, work with limited connectivity, and accommodate changing guidance. KRISHOKTECH is a Bengali agricultural advisory system built around an explicit authorization boundary around generation. Before retrieval, normalization and rule-based admission checks refer policy-covered high-risk requests and ask for a crop when treatment intent is underspecified. The system then binds retrieval to a single crop and asks for confirmation when the text and image indicate different crops. After generation, a narrow verifier removes dosage claims not supported by retrieved BARI/BRRI evidence. Agricultural guidance is kept in an external evidence index that can be updated without retraining the generator, while browser-side vision and local retrieval reduce connectivity requirements. The interface makes these decisions visible as ASK, CONFIRM, REFER, and DROP, together with their evidence. On 200 farmer queries and 400 stress queries, the controls halted underspecified requests and reduced cross-crop retrieval violations from 36.5% to 0% under the tested alias filter. Mismatch detection caught 453 of 454 text-image conflicts, while the verifier caught 114 of 118 inserted dosage errors. The demonstration shows how these controls govern the path from request to delivered advice.
ndaacb23e65b8: We study the fundamental problem of PAC learning positive linear combinations of $k$ arbitrary ReLU activations on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with respect to the Gaussian distribution, in $L_2$ loss. We give the first fully-polynomial time algorithm for this learning task. Specifically, our algorithm draws $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/ε)$ samples, runs in $\mathrm{poly}(d, k, 1/ε)$ time, and outputs a hypothesis that is $ε$-close to the target concept with high probability. All prior algorithms for this problem require super-polynomial time in $k$ or $1/ε$, or leverage strong well-conditioned assumptions on the weight matrix. On a technical level, our approach develops a novel boosting procedure of a ``weak'' learner that recovers the hidden weight vectors to constant error, in a list-decodable manner. To develop this ``weak'' learning procedure, we leverage implicit tensor computation techniques to construct a low-degree filtering procedure based on Hermite tensors of the target function. This procedure amplifies separation among (clusters of) weight vectors to learn each of them to constant error. We then argue that the same procedure can be used for improving the estimation of hidden weight vectors, using gradient descent-like updates on the Euclidean sphere. A crucial ingredient of our algorithm is a pruning approach that ensures only relevant vectors that approximate the hidden weight vectors at target accuracy are maintained by the algorithm.
nc2663ace564c: Location encoders map geographic coordinates to high-dimensional descriptors through contrastive alignment with paired Earth Observation imagery. We prove that this construction is structurally limited: any Lipschitz location encoder produces an output of intrinsic dimension at most 2, regardless of architecture or bandwidth, which forces the contrastive loss to strictly exceed its asymptotic optimum. Empirically, joint training also collapses the encoder's embedding covariance to low rank. Although dimension-limited, current location encoders sidestep this spectral collapse by training against a frozen image encoder, which we reinterpret as a covariance regularizer that supplies a high-rank target for the location encoder to fold onto. However, extending this approach to multimodal inputs is challenging, as location encoders should simultaneously map a single location to multiple, potentially incompatible, descriptors. We identify two requirements a regularizer must satisfy for location encoding in multimodal regimes: co-alignment across modalities, since adapters alone cannot align independently pretrained encoders; and high effective rank, since the location encoder inherits its target's spectrum. We propose LoCA (Location Contrastive Alignment), a two-stage pipeline that satisfies both. Stage 1 jointly trains Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 encoders with contrastive learning, producing a co-aligned, high-rank multimodal target. Stage 2 freezes the image encoders and trains a location and a tabular metadata encoder as projection adapters with multi-view contrastive learning. Against five state-of-the-art encoders on 17 tasks ranging from land cover and wildfire forecasting to geophysical, socio-economic, biodiversity and climate applications, LoCA achieves the most task wins, is the only model to outperform every other on a majority of tasks, and wins 68.8% of all per-task comparisons.
nb3b01a3edfec: Personal email agents decide, for every message, what it is, whether it is urgent, whether to draft a reply, create a task, or ignore it. Their error rate is rarely measured: the stored labels were written by the system itself. We present Foyer, a self-hosted personal inbox agent in daily use, and a measurement protocol (stratified sampling, frozen snapshots, thread-grouped splits, pre-registered hypotheses, human labels in the agent's review loop) that yields ground truth before any training. On 739 real Italian/English emails labelled by the owner (231 unbiased, 500 adversarially sampled), we compare nine systems under thread-grouped cross-validation: the production keyword rules, a TF-IDF + logistic-regression baseline, local typed decision models (Tev1, Nimble), a hosted decision model (Nimble v4-max), and hosted generative LLMs (Qwen2.5-7B, Gemma 4 26B/31B). Four results. The production rules score 28% on message type against a 58% majority class: the field shown most prominently carried no information. With ~200 labels, logistic regression has the highest accuracy on every field (type 0.79, urgency 0.74, needs-reply 0.83, is-noise 0.90), though it never predicts the two rarest classes and is statistically tied with Gemma 4 on type; few-shot prompting does not close the gap. The sender's relationship (client, supplier, service) is recovered from other emails of the same contact with 98.6% accuracy where the contact has been seen, and is not inferable from a single message by any model: it belongs in the contact graph, not the prompt. Finally, accuracy is not the product metric: composed into actions, the most accurate system most often ignores emails needing action (18% vs 4% for the best LLM); a cost-chosen threshold on its noise probability halves that rate and makes it the cheapest system.
na093e9269370: Large language model (LLM) platforms introducing advertising must decide how much capability ad revenue should fund and what consumers should pay to avoid ads. We study a monopolistic platform that jointly chooses costly response quality, advertising intensity, and subscription prices when advertising reduces user value but better service raises advertising returns. Three findings follow. First, when partly ad-supported and ad-free plans coexist, advertising can finance useful service for consumers who receive none under pure subscription. Lower effective quality in middle plans weakens the alternatives available to premium users, allowing higher prices for unchanged ad-free service. Some fully ad-supported users gain utility, while partly ad-supported and ad-free users lose: broader access can coexist with utility polarization. Second, an intermediate advertising cap can maximize consumer surplus by preserving some revenue that finances service while limiting degradation. Third, cheaper compute can raise quality and reduce ad intensity, yet sufficiently large cost reductions can increase aggregate advertising revenue above its initial level because better service raises the value of the remaining advertised interactions. An extension shows how advertising-funded upgrades can bring plans to the same maximum capability and advertising exposure, eliminating the basis for different prices. These results make menu design central to evaluating LLM advertising: the consequences extend beyond users who see ads to the alternatives and prices faced by those who do not.
nb314caa3e3f3: We learn schedules for a continuous penalty relaxation of MAX-CUT by backpropagating through an unrolled classical solver. A state-blind schedule generalizes to instances substantially larger than those used for training. A state-adaptive bilinear schedule also generalizes out of distribution, outperforming its untrained baseline across 15 seeds ($t=4.1$). By contrast, an additive ablation with identical inputs and output heads is statistically indistinguishable from the bilinear model in distribution but performs worse than its own baseline out of distribution ($t=-11.7$). This separation appears without regularization and persists across a $30$ round weight-decay sweep: the bilinear advantage remains significant at every tested value, whereas the additive model never recovers. The results in this setting isolate how solver state enters the schedule, rather than state adaptivity alone, as the architectural distinction associated with out-of-distribution transfer.
ncea493069f37: We study the list replicability number in the realizable PAC learning framework and prove that every concept class $H$ over a countable domain with Littlestone dimension $d$ and dual VC dimension $v^*$ satisfies \[ \mathrm{LR}(H)\leq 2^{O(d\min\{\log d,v^*\})}. \] This matches the worst-case lower bound of $2^{Ω(d)}$ up to a logarithmic factor in the exponent and exponentially improves the previous best upper bound $\mathrm{LR}(H)\le 2^{2^{O(d)}}$ of Bun, Livni, and Moran [FOCS 2020]. Unlike earlier bounds of $2^{O_ε(d^2)}$ for fixed accuracy $ε>0$ implied by the work of Ghazi, Golowich, Kumar, and Manurangsi [STOC 2021] and Lyu [STOC 2026], our bound is independent of $ε$. The $2^{O(d\log d)}$ bound follows from a new inductive framework for bounding list replicability that builds on the recent notion of irreducibility from differentially private learning. The $2^{O(dv^*)}$ bound follows from a simple globally stable learner that takes the majority vote of multiple empirical risk minimizers, with stability established using tools from stable regularity.
n33ffb1bd101c: During joint training, backpropagation allows later layers to reshape earlier representations, a feedback mechanism absent from purely layer-wise learning. We extend Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a recently proposed layer-wise spectral surrogate for feature learning, to capture this interaction. Starting from the exact backpropagation gradients, we derive a local coupling between a neuron's incoming weights and its corresponding next-layer column. In a controlled small-initialization regime with smooth activations and fixed surroundings, these dynamics amplify singular modes of a cross-layer correlation operator. Each growing mode pairs an earlier feature with an upper-layer response through shared neuron coefficients. This motivates a backward-coupling algorithm in which upper-layer sensitivities generate sample-dependent effective labels for earlier spectral steps, while corrected features refine upward transmission. A function-space variational principle characterizes the selected feature-response pairs by maximizing the label correlation of their product under kernel-norm constraints. For three-layer networks, we derive self-consistent continuous-time dynamics for the filtered hidden-layer features, the activation kernels, and the network output under the proposed backward coupling. In a hierarchical multi-index model, we establish a feature-recovery separation: backward coupling recovers lower-layer directions invisible to the original forward label-weighted statistic. The linear specialization recovers residual-dependent singular-mode dynamics, while paired modes provide a dynamical mechanism for linked low-rank covariance components consistent with the rainbow-network picture. Experiments with fully connected and convolutional networks on binary CIFAR-10 show improved accuracy over forward Neural LoFi at matched widths.
na4ee438816f9: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.
ne877d196d2f1: Sparse linear regression is a fundamental problem in high-dimensional statistics, and its private counterparts leave a large gap between the central and the local model of differential privacy. Shuffled differential privacy (SDP) sits between the two, offering accuracy closer to the central model without the trust requirement of a central curator. This paper studies sparse linear regression under both non-interactive and interactive SDP protocols. In the non-interactive setting, any non-interactive $(ε,δ)$-SDP protocol is shown to incur an $\ell_2$-norm estimation error of $Ω( \frac{\sqrt{dk}}{nε} )$ with dimension $d$, sparsity $k$, and $n$ users, revealing an inherent dimensionality barrier. In addition, a non-interactive algorithm is proposed that achieves an $\ell_2$-norm upper bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \sqrt{\frac{k}{n}} + \frac{d\sqrt{k}}{nε})$. To overcome this barrier, we turn to the interactive user-level setting, where each user holds $m$ samples. A two-round interactive algorithm is developed that first recovers the support through a heavy hitter step and then estimates the parameter, achieving an error of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}( \sqrt{\frac{k}{nm}} + \frac{k}{n\sqrt{m}ε} )$ with no polynomial dependence on $d$. Furthermore, by extending the score attack framework to user-level data, a new lower bound $Ω( \sqrt{\frac{k\log(d/k)}{nm}} + \frac{k\log(d/k)}{n\sqrt{m}ε} )$ is established for any user-level $(ε,δ)$-DP, showing that the proposed algorithm is near-optimal with only a gap of the factor $\log(d/k)$.
nd13f1a2e62e3: Over the past fifteen years, digital tools for parallelizing and aligning textual corpora have developed significantly within the field of digital humanities. Several projects and software tools have been created to compare different translations or versions of texts. Despite these technical advances, many parallel corpora produced in academic contexts quickly become inaccessible online due to the lack of maintenance or funding. To address this gap, we present a suite of open-source tools developed within the ACR Grimm Tradalign and ParaTaxe projects. This suite includes the AIlign aligner, based on multilingual embeddings, a Python processing pipeline for converting and aligning corpora, a web interface called ParaTaxe for managing collections of parallel corpora, and a web interface for exploring aligned corpora built with TEI-Publisher.
nf21dfe220764: This work introduces PoKER, a novel probabilistic model engineered to optimize missile launch effectiveness in air-to-air scenarios, specifically within Beyond Visual Range (BVR) air combat. Unlike conventional Weapon Engagement Zone (WEZ) models that delineate zones based on static distances such as maximum, minimum, and no-escape ranges, PoKER applies machine learning to predict kill probabilities more accurately by integrating the stochastic behaviors of targets and missile miss distances. This model dynamically evaluates target behavior, greatly expanding the predictive capabilities of engagement analysis. By factoring in elements such as warhead lethality, target and shooter orientations, and the specific conditions of engagement, PoKER provides important insights into engagement dynamics and quantifies success probabilities. Consequently, it can potentially be an important tool for BVR air combat pilots, improving operational decision-making within this specialized combat domain.
nd5da188c3e97: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms rely on estimators, like Monte Carlo tree search or one-step look-ahead, to provide policy, value, or Q-value estimates in training and inference. However, existing bandit-based estimation frameworks evaluate sampling efficiency, not the quality of estimates. We address this by formalising estimate generation as a recommendation process, treating bandit-based sampling as an improvement operator. To evaluate the quality of a recommendation (estimate), we define regulariser-aware recommender regrets, analysing their lower bounds, and proving that simple algorithms like uniform sampling can achieve these bounds. Finally, we unify bandit- and search-based target improvement under recommender MCTS. Across synthetic trees, arcade games, and scientific discovery tasks, recommenders often yield faster target convergence and superior downstream performance. Our experiments characterise for the first time the potential of regularised MCTS in scientific applications.
nb4721fe497b9: Regularised reinforcement learning (RL) has provable robustness guarantees that should ease the transfer of policies from simulation to robots, known as sim-to-real. Yet, weakly regularised algorithms like Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) remain the de facto choice in sim-to-real pipelines, while the practical benefits of regularisation for transfer remain poorly characterised. In this work, we study the sim-to-real performance of commonly used RL algorithms, with the aim of characterising the effects of regularisation on robotic performance. To that end, we derive Soft MellowMax Actor-Critic (SMM-AC), a novel regularised RL algorithm based on the soft mellowmax value function, which carries strong robustness guarantees. On MuJoCo continuous control benchmarks, SMM-AC is competitive with baselines like Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). On real robots, SMM-AC achieves higher return, while exhibiting greater robustness to perturbations in observations, the environment, and dynamics than baselines. Together, these results demonstrate that regularised RL improves real-world policy deployment through better robustness to the sim-to-real gap, and changing real-world conditions.
nb30bbb176b88: Enterprises are deploying agentic AI across the software development lifecycle, and they need the behavioral logic of the systems they act on, not stakeholder documentation. A seven-agent reverse-engineering pipeline recovered this logic, processing 241 repositories across 18 services into thousands of artifacts describing scope, journeys, rules and acceptance criteria. Recovery does not confer usability. Entities like offer, eligibility, and activation recur across services under a shared vocabulary, related in name but operationally distinct, so one end-to-end journey implicates over a thousand near-identical rules that must not be conflated. Flat vector retrieval fails, returning an identical rule from the wrong service at high similarity with no signal of error. Content-level ontology, the traditional remedy, did not exist, and relating every occurrence of recurring entities would have cost more than the engagement and not survived a release cycle. We place the ontology at the artifact level. In this machine-generated corpus, each artifact retains its producer, component, service, domain and type, provenance that disambiguates before content is read. We present a knowledge layer that organizes before retrieving: a self-describing catalog, a sparse metadata registry, and a navigation hypergraph defined over artifacts rather than extracted entities. Queries resolve to artifact identifiers that constrain vector search, so the competing rule from another service is absent rather than outranked, making disambiguation structural, not statistical. Built in under a week and admitting new services by convention, the layer serves SDLC agents, developers, quality engineers and analysts. It supported root-cause analysis and resolution of 100+ production defects with developer verification and attributed 35 release regression failures to specific rules and services.
n0e91667309b7: Multi-step predictions of future transition realizations can improve reinforcement learning, but their value remains difficult to quantify. Directly including these predictions in the state can lead to exponential state-space growth, making direct dynamic programming computationally expensive. We study discounted finite MDPs under a block-feedback protocol: at the start of each K-period block, the decision maker observes $K$-step probabilistic transition predictions for a subset of actions and adapts decisions to observed states within the block. We show that the optimal value satisfies a Bayesian Bellman equation on the original state space. This representation reveals that predictive information creates value by recursively changing the local order of maximization and expectation in the Bellman expansion. We formalize this effect through a Bellman--Jensen analysis and quantify the effects of prediction horizon, error, action coverage, and within-block feedback. We propose block-feedback Bayesian offline learning with online adaptation (BF--BOLA), a model-based algorithm for learning near-optimal policies, and establish upper and lower sample-complexity bounds that match up to logarithmic factors in the stated regimes. The results show that predictions can reduce transition learning to uncovered rows and that learning a near-optimal policy can require fewer prediction samples than estimating the Bayesian value function.
ncdff46e63630: Robust reinforcement learning (RL) is critical for reliable real-world deployment, where policies may fail under diverse shifts and disruptions. Existing robust RL algorithms offer a rich set of mechanisms and principles, yet two major barriers limit their broader potential: limited algorithm reusability and an unclear empirical capability boundary. We introduce RobustRLlib, an algorithm-centric library and benchmark that addresses both challenges. It integrates 17 representative robust online, offline, and safe RL algorithms under a unified interface for substantially improved reusability, together with an enhanced evaluation platform spanning diverse real-world shifts and advanced humanoid and vision-language-action tasks. Systematic evaluation over 273 perturbation configurations provides an up-to-date capability map of current robust RL algorithms, revealing where they remain effective and where substantial robustness gaps persist. As an open-source, user-friendly platform, RobustRLlib offers a reproducible and extensible codebase for applying existing methods to new problems and developing new robust RL algorithms.
n98aaf0b9f798: Modern vision encoders are widely used as semantic representations, but the relationship between embedding similarity and human-visible semantics can become unclear far from the natural-image manifold. We probe this regime in a black-box setting by applying sparse pixel edits to blank canvases with a simple pixel-level hill-climbing procedure. Across ImageNet and Flickr30k, we evaluate whether these edited blank canvases can retrieve chosen targets in multimodal contrastive encoders and self-supervised visual encoders. On OpenCLIP, inputs optimized toward class prompts achieve strong top-1 and top-5 targeted retrieval performance; on DINOv3, inputs optimized toward class prototypes achieve high target alignment and near-top prototype ranks. These results show that sparse edits on otherwise blank, visually non-semantic inputs can enter target semantic basins in both language-aligned and self-supervised visual representation spaces. Our findings identify a shared off-manifold failure mode of modern vision encoders and suggest sparse blank-canvas optimization as a simple probe of representation geometry.
neba6ba91a4bf: Training generalizable embodied agents requires realistic, varied, and simulation-ready indoor environments. Language-guided methods support semantic planning and object-level reasoning, but precise spatial grounding remains difficult. Visual generative models offer rich priors over plausible arrangements, yet their outputs require geometric reasoning to become physically valid 3D scenes. We introduce SceneBloom, an agentic framework that combines visual layout sampling with contract-guided 3D compilation. A hierarchical sampler uses diffusion priors to generate furniture arrangements within functional zones. A compiler then uses relations extracted from each proposal to guide geometric fitting and local pose correction. Across five room types, SceneBloom attains the highest visual quality and physical stability among the compared methods and is the only method with no detected mesh collisions and out-of-bounds objects. Its layouts are also closer to the distribution of real rooms than those of all compared baselines. Object navigation policies trained in these realistic scenes achieve a higher success rate in held-out real scans than those trained on an equal number of real training scans. Code is available at https://github.com/Tinaliu0123/scenebloom.
ne8e18fd84282: Statement autoformalization translates mathematics from natural language into a proof assistant such as Lean 4, and models now do it at scale. As provers get stronger, the burden of correctness shifts from the proof to the statement, that is, to whether the formal statement faithfully translates its source. Given a trusted reference formalization, the natural test is logical equivalence, and it proves too much. $P \leftrightarrow Q$ holds trivially for any two statements $P$ and $Q$ that the library proves, because a prover can prove each separately and pass through $P \leftrightarrow \mathrm{True} \leftrightarrow Q$. The stronger the prover, the more unrelated pairs pass. Earlier methods restrict the prover and check that each proof names the other statement. We introduce SemantEq, a more principled relation that instead requires each statement to turn into the other only through a chain of allowed steps, such as logical rearrangement and rewriting with the library's own equations. Our programs judge a proof by the proof term Lean checks, not by its tactic script.
