SemantEq-Eval, a search without a model, reaches 100% precision and 65.6% recall on the ProofNetVerif test split under our adjudicated labels, against 95.8% and 61.8% for BEq+, and an 8.9-fold increase in its CPU time adds at most three pairs. A language model finds more proofs, but under two of four prompts it proves both directions of about two in five of the non-equivalent pairs. SemantEq-ProofAudit audits each model-written proof under a policy derived from the relation and accepts none of the 104 non-equivalent pairs, and it raises recall on 407 equivalent pairs from 65.4% to 81.1% under the best prompt. Separating the generation of equivalence proofs from their acceptance lets a stronger prover raise recall without changing what an acceptance means. We release code and data at: https://github.com/hlxr89/SemantEq
nb8de2368d32a: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is now a standard approach to parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks. Its low-rank factorization is inherently non-identifiable, making LoRA a singular statistical model whose learning complexity cannot be described by parameter dimension alone. We study this complexity using the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) from singular learning theory and how it depends on both the low-rank parameterization and the pretrained network. Under a local linearization, LoRA induces a low-rank trace regression model whose Kullback--Leibler geometry is controlled by a forward-backward covariance, constructed from activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer. This covariance determines which low-rank perturbations are statistically observable. When it is nondegenerate along the relevant low-rank directions, we recover the classical learning complexity of reduced-rank regression; when its kernel meets these directions, additional statistically indistinguishable parameters change the singular geometry. We characterize this geometry locally through observable tangent directions and a residual singularity, and globally through affine linear sections of determinantal varieties. The global learning complexity need not be determined at a ground-truth parameter, as singularities on another rank stratum can dominate. We also introduce a curvature-corrected multi-temperature estimator of the RLCT. Experiments on multilayer perceptron and transformer architectures reveal strongly layer-dependent forward-backward geometry and show that ambient covariance degeneracy does not imply degeneracy along the low-rank directions relevant to adaptation.
nccc2347131ac: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) offer strong zero-shot forecasting capabilities, but their high pretraining cost raises a practical sustainability question: does this upfront investment pay off over a full deployment lifecycle, compared to supervised standalone models that must be periodically retrained? We model the cumulative carbon cost of different approaches across a realistic industrial scenario: Chronos-2 amortizes its pretraining cost within months for large or frequently queried deployments, but a classical model remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried ones. For cases where reducing the TSFM's own cost matters, we show that removing a single encoder block (7.9% of parameters) via a gradient-free pruning criterion yields a consistent 6 to 9% reduction in FLOPs, CO2 emissions, and latency, at essentially no cost to zero-shot forecasting performance across a 25-task benchmark.
nc03c7422f5ee: This article argues that instruction-fine-tuned language models should be understood as implementing a genre, what is proposed as the instructional-conversational genre. This genre is an amalgamation of discursive language from prior conversations between generative models and humans recursively run through these massive neural networks. It is instantiated in applications through instruction fine-tuning, the inclusion of a pretext known as a system prompt, and the formalization of inputs in mark-up languages characterized by the use of special tokens and role assignment in turntaking structures.
na4484b1dfe85: Pipelines that combine large language models (LLMs) with static analysis let the model consume the analyser's output as evidence, but whether the model distinguishes true from false evidence, and whether its scrutiny depends on what the evidence claims, has not been measured. We built an intraprocedural analyser for C/C++ that produces proof obligations and audited vulnerable and patched functions from PrimeVul under six evidence conditions that differ only in the notes, including fabricated assurances that a missing check exists and fabricated alarms that an added check is missing. The study covers 916 pairs in four disjoint sets, eleven model configurations from four vendors and 16,572 audits; no model is trained or fine-tuned. True evidence barely improved accuracy (+0.02). False evidence acted asymmetrically: relative to true notes about the same operations, false assurances lowered the detection of real vulnerabilities by up to 19 points, whereas false alarms never significantly lowered accuracy and were disputed far more often. An internally registered replication on seven new models confirmed that false assurances move verdicts towards their claim more than false alarms do (mean asymmetry +0.16, 95% CI +0.10 to +0.24). Instructions in the audit prompt did not reliably reduce deference; the best one failed to replicate. Verifying each claim in a separate call and showing the refuted claims raised accuracy under false assurances by 12 points in a pre-specified test (p=0.002) without loss under true evidence; for a second model the gain was smaller and not significant. Pipelines should therefore verify a tool's guarantees before the model relies on them, and studies should measure deference in a direction-aware way.
n18fe5c0c054c: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.
nf627f48ee8ac: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies can adapt to local human intervention, while federated learning can combine distributed robot experience without pooling raw records. We examine their prospective intersection: sharing adaptations derived from diverse human corrections across tasks, environments, people, and robot embodiments. Corrections differ in modality, safety semantics(urgency, behavioral scope, etc.), and privacy sensitivity. A shared update that improves mean task success may suppress a rare safety intervention or produce an unsafe response on another robot. We argue for three requirements: preserve the context and uncertainty of multimodal corrections when deciding what to share; assess candidate updates in each receiving robot's closed loop before deployment; and evaluate leakage alongside retention of safety-critical evidence. Immediate, legible defensive behavior remains necessary during human interaction. We offer counterexamples and a falsifiable evaluation agenda, not experimental results.
n65fbed655371: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. Even with identical weights and BF16 tensors, implementation differences can make an intended on-policy update off-policy and destabilize training. Existing remedies align the entire inference and training stacks, change global precision, or modify the learning algorithm. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. We align training-side rounding locations with inference in three regions---RoPE, SwiGLU, and residual RMSNorm---by retaining selected intermediates in FP32 until their BF16 outputs. Across four Qwen-family models, aligning all three regions prevents the collapse observed under the default BF16 baseline; RoPE-path alignment alone also suffices in the studied runs, despite remaining numerical discrepancies. The interventions keep the inference engine, matrix-multiplication and attention kernels, and learning objective unchanged.
n292b86919e55: Despite advances in multilingual text representations, effective dense retrieval for Persian remains constrained by the limited availability of language-specific training resources and compact embedding models. We present Yalda Embedding, a 595.8-million-parameter Persian retrieval model adapted from Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B using more than one million query-document pairs. On eight Persian retrieval tasks from FaMTEB, the model achieves the highest macro-average among the evaluated 0.6B models, scoring 0.5488 and outperforming Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and F2LLM-v2-0.6B on every task. It also approaches Qwen3-Embedding-4B, winning on four tasks, tying on one, and trailing by 0.0075 in macro-average. An incremental ablation study examines contrastive batch size, optimization stabilization, and relational knowledge distillation from F2LLM-v2-8B. Under the one-epoch training setup, contrastive fine-tuning alone yields a modest mean improvement over initialization and regressions on two tasks. The final distilled configuration improves all eight tasks over the non-distilled model, raising the mean from 0.4813 to 0.5488 without increasing inference-time model size. These gains include hard-negative evaluation tasks despite training without explicitly mined or supplied hard negatives. We release model weights, training and evaluation code, the pairwise dataset, and its teacher-embedded counterpart, enabling inspection of data composition and training procedures, independent evaluation, and reuse without repeating expensive teacher inference.
n0d1bc502391a: State inference and parameter learning for nonlinear filters is a core computation for scientific machine learning with varied applications in engineering and neuroscience. The unnormalized filtering distribution is governed by the Zakai equation, a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) that combines the forward Kolmogorov operator (known as the Fokker-Planck equation) with observed likelihood updates. Although solving these high-dimensional SPDEs is often impossible analytically and intractable numerically, advances in operator learning and physics-informed machine learning have made it feasible. Harnessing these advances, we introduce the Zakai Equation Neural Operator (ZENO), a model that optimizes a neural operator against a Zakai Equation based physics-informed loss to approximate the exact unnormalized filtering distribution for latent stochastic dynamical systems. We use this ZENO-inferred posterior distribution in an expectation-maximization (EM) framework to perform parameter learning and state inference. We demonstrate ZENO's ability to accurately infer the posterior distribution and learn its corresponding SDE parameters in three simulated stochastic dynamical systems (Double-Well bistable system, Van Der Pol (VDP) oscillator, and Lorenz system) and compare its performance against established methods for latent SDE inference and learning. We show that ZENO recovers previously observed limit cycles representing forward and backward locomotion from a whole-brain imaging dataset of immobilized \textit{C. elegans} nematodes. ZENO is a novel approach to the problem of nonlinear filtering and dynamical inference through the lens of partial differential equations and operator theory.
n2dbd82545fa4: The classical theory of p-n junctions derives the current-voltage characteristic from minority-carrier diffusion alone: majority carriers are treated as an inert background, the quasi-neutral base as field-free, and the junction voltage as equal to the applied bias. These premises fail together under high bias and high-level injection, where the observed current roll-off is reproduced only by appending an empirical series resistance outside the junction physics. Here we develop a self-consistent two-carrier drift-diffusion framework that introduces no assumption beyond the classical ones. Excess majority carriers are shown to be electrostatically forced transport participants: the ambipolar diffusion equation, closed by exact two-sided boundary conditions, yields a unified excess-carrier profile. The resulting base field separates into an ohmic and a Dember component, and all four current components follow in closed form, their sum being position independent. At device level the framework closes into an extended diode equation that contains the Shockley equation as its low-injection, long-base limit and reproduces the n=2 roll-off intrinsically. The junction voltage emerges as a self-limiting drop confined to the space-charge region and separated from the applied bias by exact base drops. Two device-level corrections are quantified: at high current, 75-90% of the dissipation migrates from the junction into the quasi-neutral base, and field-assisted acceleration shortens the base transit time by up to a factor of six. Three parameter-free predictions follow: a universal ideality-factor crossover that passes through 3/2 when the boundary excess equals the doping, a high-injection onset voltage that scales as 119 mV per decade of doping, and a geometry factor that survives into high injection.
nef896abe24fa: Recent work has introduced the notion of a time semicrystal, a driven nonequilibrium regime in which subharmonic temporal order survives inside deterministic chaos. Here we revisit this phenomenology from the viewpoint of classical nonlinear dynamics. Banded chaotic attractors consist of a finite number of chaotic sectors cyclically permuted by stroboscopic evolution, allowing discrete subharmonic spectral components to coexist with a broadband chaotic continuum. Exemplified through the driven Duffing oscillator and the logistic map, this structure naturally reproduces the characteristic signatures of time-semicrystalline dynamics. Within this framework, periodic subharmonic motion can enter chaos through the familiar period-doubling cascade while retaining a well-defined temporal skeleton governed by the universal Feigenbaum scaling. Temporal order within chaos can also reorganize or collapse through distinct mechanisms, producing continuous or abrupt transitions that may be intertwined with symmetry changes. These results connect time-semicrystal phenomenology with established structures of dissipative nonlinear dynamics, showing that its essential ingredients already arise in standard nonlinear systems and providing a simple framework for extending and testing the paradigm in more complex, many-body, and experimental settings.
n958f8623cf5e: We investigate how the shape and arrangement of high-stiffness regions govern stress redistribution in two-component triangular elastic spring networks subjected to spatially correlated and uncorrelated random prestress. We compare boundary roughness, partitioning into disconnected regions, and graded transitions between regions of different stiffness. Our simulations identify interface bonds as channels for energy transfer: increasing their number provides additional transfer paths and reduces stress concentration in mechanically rigid regimes, while offering little benefit in compliant subnetworks. This is analogous to defects in naturally occurring crystal structures, where the defects themselves isolate stress. At a fixed fraction of high-stiffness material, partitioning reduces stress concentration for both correlated and uncorrelated prestress. The benefit diminishes with further subdivision as the number of interface bonds becomes comparable to the number of interior nodes. Stress reduction, however, depends on the spatial correlations of the imposed prestress: random prestress generally yields a stronger effect, though the difference diminishes in some regimes. Graded interfaces further reduce peak stress by distributing the stiffness transition over a broader region. Together, these results suggest design strategies based on increasing interface area, matching subdivision scale to prestress correlations, and grading stiffness transitions. This minimal framework identifies how internal structure controls energy transfer and stress redistribution, suggesting design principles for mechanical robustness under both internal and external loading.
n06890a20d8b8: The square-lattice compass model is a paradigm of bond-dependent frustration, yet experimental evidence for its characteristic spin correlations has remained elusive. Here we identify compass correlations in the square-lattice intermetallic ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ using single-crystal neutron diffuse scattering. Comparative measurements on the isostructural compounds NdRu$_2$Si$_2$ and ErRu$_2$Si$_2$ reveal a pronounced contrast between nearly uniform diffuse rings in the former and strong intensity modulation between Brillouin zones in the latter. Through the magnetic neutron polarization factor, this modulation reveals compass correlations that couple moment orientation to the correlation wavevector. Crystal-field spectroscopy identifies four preferred in-plane orientations for the Er$^{3+}$ moments. A minimal compass-Heisenberg model incorporating this anisotropy quantitatively reproduces the diffuse scattering and accounts for the double-$Q$ vortex-antivortex ground state. Fits with the compass couplings fixed at values set by the dipolar energy scale retain good agreement with the data, supporting a substantial dipolar contribution to the bond-dependent interactions. Our results establish a square-lattice platform for compass physics and suggest that dipolar interactions, acting together with local crystal-field anisotropy, can shape directional magnetic correlations alongside conduction-electron-mediated exchange.
nc302b24d904d: Transport measurements on lithographically patterned graphene nanoribbons suggest that the gap depends primarily on ribbon width rather than on crystallographic edge orientation, in contrast to predictions of ideal tight-binding models. To address this, we develop a transfer-matrix approach, based on the theory of finite periodic systems, in which each carbon atom of the honeycomb lattice is represented by an individual $δ$-scatterer with interaction strength $γ^{}_δ$ and the nanoribbon is treated as a confined multichannel finite periodic system. We derive the unit-cell transfer matrix for both arm-chair and zig-zag edge configurations and obtain the transmission and channel-coupling coefficients in closed form. The transmission spectra display the resonant band structure characteristic of finite periodic systems, with the number of resonances per allowed band increasing with the number of unit cells. For $γ_δ=0$ the ribbons are fully transparent; for $γ_δ>0$ a low-energy transport gap opens and grows linearly with the scatterer strength, $Δ=0.364265\,γ_δ$, identically for arm-chair and zig-zag edges. These results are consistent with the reported absence of a systematic dependence on orientation, while the analytical results show that interchannel coupling vanishes exactly for arm-chair ribbons and decreases with increasing width for zig-zag ribbons, revealing the role of edge geometry. Together, these findings indicate that atomic-scale scattering, represented by the $δ$-potential formalism, provides a common orientation-independent contribution to the low-energy transport gap in the pristine ribbons considered here.
nd1588eed604e: We extend the discrete WKB method to one-dimensional bipartite tight-binding chains of free fermions with slowly varying hopping amplitudes and on-site potentials. We focus on the inhomogeneous Rice-Mele model, suggesting possible experimental realizations thereof in optical superlattices. We derive explicit semiclassical expressions for the single-particle wave functions and density of states, as well as the sublattice-resolved local particle densities and filling fraction at arbitrary Fermi energy. In particular, we show that the WKB density profiles agree with those obtained from the local-density approximation. We analyze the spatial dependence of the local band edges and its consequences for the global spectral structure, and clarify the role played by the phase-space topology in determining the Bohr-Sommerfeld quantization conditions. Finally, we illustrate our results with two representative examples: a homogeneous Rice-Mele chain subject to a harmonic trap and a fully inhomogeneous chain containing a domain wall.
n03b4fc510afa: Surface oxidation is a common concern for ultrathin NbN superconducting devices, yet which superconducting properties it affects has not been established for films grown by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition. We expose NbN films about 11.4 nm thick to an O$_2$ plasma for 0 to 60 s, which oxidizes the surface without etching the film, and characterize the same sample series by X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), and transport measurements on 500 nm wide nanowires. XPS of the surface and the underlying layer shows that the plasma converts the surface to Nb$_2$O$_5$, whereas the bulk of the treated film is chemically identical to that of the untreated film. Crystalline $\delta$-NbN remains intact. During exposure, the total film thickness rises and saturates between 40 and 60 s, indicating self-limiting surface oxide growth. The normal-state resistivity rises by 21% (dc) and 25% (optical) with the plasma dose, while the critical temperature and transition width are unchanged. The switching current densities of 4.9-6.2 MA/cm$^2$ at 4.2 K show no systematic dependence on the plasma dose. Their temperature dependence follows the dirty-limit depairing current of Kupriyanov and Lukichev, and the extrapolated switching currents reach 39-46% of the depairing current calculated from the optical resistivity and diffusion coefficient, in agreement with the width dependence reported for nanowires from the same process. The oxygen signature is confined to temperatures near $T_c$, where the supercurrent of the treated wires vanishes at least 0.5 K earlier than that of the untreated wire, consistent with a partially oxidized surface layer that acts on the film by the proximity effect. At these doses, oxygen narrows the temperature range of the supercurrent from above but does not systematically reduce the low-temperature current-carrying capacity of the wires.
n937f9b62918d: We investigate how symmetry-breaking boundary magnetic fields affect magnetization and Rényi-2 entanglement asymmetry (EA) in the transverse-field Ising model. For the ground state, magnetization exhibits qualitatively distinct behaviors in the ordered and disordered phases. EA also exhibits phase-dependent behavior, which is well captured by the lower and upper bounds derived in this work. In the critical regime, both magnetization and EA exhibit behavior qualitatively consistent with the field-theoretical predictions for a related setup. We also study boundary-quench dynamics and find that magnetization propagates from the boundary into the bulk with a velocity consistent with the maximum quasiparticle velocity. In contrast, because EA is a subsystem-integrated quantity, its spatial structure is not directly resolved. We therefore introduce the asymmetry contour, a contour-like finite-difference quantity that provides a spatially resolved characterization of the symmetry-breaking information encoded in the reduced density matrix. The resulting contour is complementary to the local magnetization, retaining sensitivity to nonlocal many-body correlations while its dynamics also reflects the underlying quasiparticle propagation. These results show how EA and its contour can provide complementary information-theoretic characterizations of symmetry breaking and its spatial structure.
n90dc8596546f: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge transfer, where quantum capacitance modifies the internal electrostatics. Using interlayer excitons as local probes, we observe a dipole-dependent energy splitting that persists even when the gate-induced geometric field is nominally canceled. This splitting reflects incomplete cancellation between gate- and carrier-induced fields set by quantum capacitance, while many-body renormalization is largely symmetric with respect to the two opposite dipole orientations, allowing the splitting to provide a direct optical measure of the local chemical potential. Our results reveal the central role of quantum capacitance in interface electrostatics and provide a route to probe it in operando.
nd5ad9811172a: Access to hydro and quasi-hydro regimes in magnetic systems is steadily increasing with the advances in fabrication of clean materials, and motivates study of hydrodynamics beyond conventional regimes and probe non-equilibrium transport. We employ the framework of extended irreversible thermodynamics which includes dynamical dissipative currents as quasi-hydro variables, and effect the modified hydrodynamic equations suitable to describe planar Heisenberg ferromagnetic systems in both paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases. We show that the new transport coefficients and relaxation time scales introduced by quasi-hydro variables can engineer diverse combination of dispersion relations and provide control over the nature of hydrodynamic modes. For instance, we can change the diffusive energy mode into propagating one in multiple ways, including by tuning the relaxation time of magnetization current.
n4d7b4466f8fe: We investigate the field-directed assembly of patchy colloidal particles composed of magnetic hematite cubes encapsulated in TPM shells. These Pacman-like particles exhibit specific interactions via their magnetic patch, enabling tunable structures under external fields. A magnetic field drives patch-to-patch interactions, while an AC electric field induces stacking and spreading. By using this multi-field combination and by varying field parameters, such as frequency and amplitude, we achieve programmable transitions between distinct assembly modes. Our work offers a versatile platform for designing reconfigurable colloidal architectures with potential applications in micro-robotics and smart materials.
nf4fdb7c3c722: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) provide a controllable platform for engineering topological Andreev spectra. At zero temperature, Andreev bound states (ABSs) with nonzero Chern numbers give rise to quantized transconductance between superconducting terminals. We derive the finite-temperature transconductance of MTJJs using linear-response theory. We first demonstrate the destructive role of temperature: changes in the thermal occupations of the ABSs destroy exact transconductance quantization. We then show that finite temperature can also play a constructive role by making the transconductance sensitive to finite-energy topological crossings hidden from the zero-temperature response. Our results establish the thermal limitations of transconductance quantization and identify finite-temperature transport as a probe of otherwise inaccessible topology in Andreev spectra.
n981db6913b30: The theory of conventional critical phenomena is built around the concepts of fluctuations and correlators of local observables. Here, we show that topological phase transitions can also be characterized through spatial and temporal two-point correlation functions associated with fluctuations of the electronic position operator. The key object is the antisymmetric part of the position-position correlation function, which yields the Chern number in the equal-time and equal-space limit. When the system is translationally invariant in space or time (the latter case corresponding to an equilibrium condition), these two-point correlators reduce to one-variable functions of the remaining variable. Remarkably, these functions are both reminiscent of critical behaviour, including divergent correlation times and lengths signalling the phase transitions. Away from these conditions, namely in non-periodic systems or genuinely dynamical processes, criticality is instead better captured by higher-order Chern-Chern correlators constructed from local or dynamical markers obtained as coincident-point limits of the position correlators. These higher-order Chern-Chern correlators can be seen as double Levi-Civita contractions of second-order position correlators, selecting the antisymmetric sector in each index pair. We substantiate this framework through numerical simulations and analytic calculations. Our results establish a general correlator-based description of topological phase transitions, applicable to crystalline, noncrystalline, equilibrium, and dynamical systems.

ne31f4cfd241c: Charge density wave (CDW) and superconductivity have long been recognized as competing orders. ncc7a77879a79: The Hubbard model offers a powerful minimal description of strongly correlated electrons in molecules and materials, yet it neglects effects observed in nature that give rise to a much richer variety of physics. ne61e83a619e1: While defect dynamics in condensed matter systems is widely studied and several methods are available to track the defect position over time, the formulation of dynamical models for the coupled evolution of both defect and background field quantities seems to be more challenging. nea48517abf8f: Medium and high-entropy alloys have emerged as a promising class of superconducting materials because their intrinsic chemical disorder can simultaneously enhance mechanical robustness and modify superconducting properties. n2b573e720a45: We consider a measured system $X$ containing a parameter $θ$ of interest and the problem of estimating this parameter by observing a second, coupled measurement system $Y$. n29a9fee17a2c: When the characteristic length scales of transport become comparable to the carrier mean free path, the local constitutive description breaks down. n9e9e442f8510: Understanding the microscopic behavior of materials in response to mechanical perturbations is a central challenge in soft matter, yet existing methods, which typically rely on microscopy-based imaging, often struggle with spatial heterogeneity and low signal-to-noise that are characteristic of many soft and biological materials. n15b7d8787c1f: An electron, when added to a fractional quantum Hall fluid, famously splits into fractionally charged composite-fermion quasiparticles. We show here that a high energy composite fermion carrying a fractional charge decays into a collection of particles, including quasiparticles, quasiholes, and even whole electrons.
nb9ce09daef40: We investigate the conversion between thermal and informational resources in an autonomous machine coupled to thermal reservoirs and a tape, playing the role of an information reservoir. The machine is able to perform information erasure driven by heat, and information-powered refrigeration, for which we introduce suitable efficiency definitions. We focus on the role of fluctuations in the currents and stochastic efficiencies, as well as in operation at optimal performance. The model is also extended to allow a coherent information reservoir, which is able to modify operation and performance. All in all, our work provides insights for the design and optimization of information-to-work conversion devices at small scales.
nc02741505f90: The recently discovered titanium-based kagome metal CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$, which exhibits superconductivity without an accompanying charge density wave, provides an ideal platform to investigate the intrinsic electronic structure and superconductivity. Moreover, it enables the exploration of superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit of the kagome lattice. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of biaxial mechanical strain ($\varepsilon$) on the electronic structure and superconductivity of monolayer CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ using first-principles calculations. We demonstrate that the prominent van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point can be monotonically tuned to the Fermi level by tensile strain. Furthermore, the superconducting transition temperature $T_C$ exhibits a dome-shaped dependence on strain, reaching a maximum of 3.6 K at an optimal tensile strain of $\varepsilon=+2\%$. The average superconducting gap magnitude is 0.35 meV, with an orbital-dependent and anisotropic distribution. Our results provide a detailed understanding of the superconductivity of monolayer CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ and show that strain is an effective, continuous tuning knob for manipulating the electronic structure and superconductivity.
nbd061edb2156: Predicting the properties of correlated materials and molecules often requires a many-body description that goes beyond single-particle and mean-field approximations. Tensor networks address this challenge by exploiting the entanglement structure of quantum states to construct compact, systematically improvable representations. Although developed largely for idealized model Hamiltonians, these methods are increasingly being integrated into material-specific calculations. This Perspective introduces their underlying principles and examines how network geometry, bond-dimension truncation, and approximate contraction determine the accuracy and computational reach of these approaches. We survey applications across regimes of increasing complexity, ranging from ground-state properties of quantum magnets and itinerant-fermion systems to excitation spectra, nonequilibrium dynamics, finite-temperature and open systems, and molecular electronic structure. We then examine four routes connecting these methods to real materials, including experimentally constrained models, downfolded Hamiltonians, dynamical mean-field theory with tensor network impurity solvers, and quantum embedding. Throughout, we evaluate the maturity of existing capabilities and their principal limitations, synthesizing this assessment into a practical method-selection guide. We argue that reliable materials predictions require quantifying uncertainties introduced at each stage, from constructing material-specific Hamiltonians to extracting experimentally accessible observables. Finally, we identify the algorithmic advances and reproducible computational practices needed to establish tensor networks as a routine tool for predictive materials science and quantum chemistry.
n5fdc59454da9: For more than 75 years, the p-n junction current-voltage characteristic has been derived by treating majority carriers as an inert background and conflating the junction voltage with the applied bias. Here we show that the base electric field, generated by the coupling of excess majority and minority carriers, fundamentally alters the internal potential distribution. This self-consistent framework yields a closed-form extended diode equation that reproduces the high-injection roll-off without invoking an external series resistance, thereby eliminating an empirical patch that has persisted in the classical theory.
n8d59f2e57937: Inferring constitutive laws from transient response data is a central inverse problem in soft condensed-matter physics, particularly when the relevant relaxation spectrum extends beyond the time window of a single experiment. Time-temperature superposition (TTS) constrains this problem for thermorheologically simple materials in the linear viscoelastic regime by allowing temperature to rescale the characteristic relaxation time without changing the underlying shape of the relaxation spectrum. We incorporate this constraint into a physics-informed machine-learning framework for time-resolved mechanical spectroscopy via chirp rheometry. We encode compact fractional viscoelastic models as causal convolutional features derived from the Boltzmann superposition principle, and we jointly fit multi-temperature chirp records using sparse variational Gaussian process regression. The model infers horizontal shift factors, constitutive parameters, and an observational-noise scale directly from time-domain stress-strain signals measured in the linear viscoelastic regime, without first extracting frequency-domain spectra or manually shifting separate curves. For synthetic Fractional Maxwell data, the method recovers the generating constitutive law from a prescribed model library and latent shifts over stress-noise levels from 3% to 25%. Applied to a DGEBA-IPDA epoxy dataset spanning the glass-transition regime, the pooled likelihood distinguishes competing fractional rheology models using the Bayesian information criterion. These results recast TTS master-curve construction as probabilistic inference over latent time rescaling and linear viscoelasticity, while also identifying limitations, such as homoscedastic noise and weakly informative spectral regimes.
nc548d418ca16: The partially disordered (PD) phase, in which magnetically ordered and Kondo-screened sites coexist, has been proposed as a possible ground state of geometrically frustrated heavy-fermion systems. We investigate its dynamical properties in the half-filled periodic Anderson model on a triangular lattice by calculating the dynamical spin susceptibility within the random-phase approximation built on a self-consistent Hartree-Fock solution. We show that successive quantum phase transitions from the Kondo-insulating phase to the PD phase and to a magnetically ordered phase are driven by the condensation of triplon modes originating predominantly from the Kondo-screened sites. In the PD phase, magnons and triplons coexist and hybridize, leading to characteristic level repulsion in the excitation spectrum. These results reveal how triplet excitations evolve into collective magnetic modes across the successive phase transitions and highlight the dynamical interplay between magnetic order and Kondo screening in frustrated heavy-fermion systems.
nef1579f827a9: Recent experiments have revealed unexpected mirror-symmetry breakings in the charge density-wave (CDW) state of rare-earth tritellurides, suggesting a putative ferro-axial CDW state. Here we report polarization-resolved Raman scattering measurements tracking the point-group symmetry breakings across the CDW phase transition in the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe$_3$. We show that the mirror-symmetry breakings follow closely the emergence of the CDW order, suggesting a single component CDW order parameter. Furthermore, Raman measurements in the $A_{2g}$ symmetry channel above the CDW transition temperature indicate the absence of significant ferro-axial fluctuations. We discuss the broad implications of these findings with respect to the nature of the CDW state in the tritellurides.
n52f7485c21b6: We introduce a classical trajectory method for calculating direct diatom-atom-atom ternary association re- action rates that incorporates the rotational degrees of freedom of the diatomic reactant. By treating the diatomic molecule as a rigid rotor, we include the effects of the anisotropy of the molecule-atom interaction and the dynamical effects of the rotational motion. We apply this approach to a system of experimental interest, CD+ + He + He, along with the isotopic variant CH+ + He + He -> CHHe+ + He, and examine the role of the internal, rotational degrees of freedom of the diatomic molecule. In particular, we find that in the regime where the collision energy is much smaller than the rotational energy of the entrance channel, the rotational motion leads to deviation from the classical threshold law by violating the assumptions of long-range capture theory models.
n6493c8d17352: Quantum equilibrium structure can be sampled using classical molecular dynamics with a learned effective potential for a single path-integral replica, but the primitive mean-force estimates obtained from path-integral molecular dynamics with that replica held fixed are noisy. We derive a scaled-gradient estimator with zero sampling variance for a one-dimensional harmonic oscillator and an estimated 4.7--57.5-fold reduction in constrained-sampling time for the molecular tests. The resulting potentials can be trained on these forces like standard machine-learning interatomic potentials and yield stable production simulations from which quantum expectation values of position-dependent observables are obtained as classical ensemble averages.
n3766b6d120ab: Simulating molecular excited-state processes requires resolving electronic and nuclear dynamics, but the cost of direct quantum-chemical calculations limits accessible system sizes and timescales. Machine-learning models can extend these simulations, yet they often need to be tailored to specific molecular systems and scientific objectives. Building and deploying such models requires coordinated decisions across conformational sampling, quantum-chemical labelling, model training, validation and dynamics. Here we introduce Paired agents for Unified Learning and Simulation of Excited States (PULSES), a multi-agent system that automates this workflow within expert-approved boundaries. A human expert and planner define the scientific objective, methods and decision boundaries, while an orchestrator coordinates domain agents and artifact-specific scientific assurance during execution. We evaluate PULSES on 15 computational chemistry tasks and demonstrate end-to-end applications to perylene exciton Hamiltonians, solvent-dependent biphenyl relaxation, and excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline. These results demonstrate traceable, expert-bounded construction and deployment of specialized excited-state models, while retaining scientific validation as a requirement rather than assuming that successful execution establishes correctness.
nfb8a233cd19a: Truncating the basis set is a straightforward way of reducing the computational cost of a calculation, often done by augmenting only the non-hydrogen atoms with diffuse functions. Calculations of non-covalent interactions, which require large diffuse basis sets for quantitative results, regularly employ this truncation. Herein, we assess the validity of this basis set truncation across the A24 and S66 datasets and for case study examples at a range of interaction distances. For the majority of non-covalent interactions, we find that the heavy-atom-only augmented basis sets can be safely applied as a method of reducing computational cost. However, for aliphatic-aliphatic and $π$-aliphatic type dispersion interactions, we find that lower cardinal number basis sets with full augmentation for all atoms, including hydrogen, can provide similar or even more accurate results than higher cardinal number basis sets with partial augmentation. These results emphasize that increasing basis set size and computational cost does not necessarily improve accuracy; rather, the composition of a basis set is critical to achieving highly accurate and efficient computations.
n15fdddb82181: Isotopic branching in ion-molecule reactions influences interstellar deuterium fractionation, yet its dynamics remain poorly understood for many important systems at astrophysically relevant temperatures. Here, we investigate H- and D-atom transfer in the $\mathrm{H_2O^+ + HD}$ reaction using single sympathetically cooled water ions in a cryogenic radiofrequency trap. Nondestructive identification of the products from 441 individual reaction events at a mean collision energy of 7 K reveals an $\mathrm{H_3O^+/H_2DO^+}$ product branching ratio of $1.50 \pm 0.15$ demonstrating a preferential H-atom transfer. The experiments are rationalized using quasi-classical-trajectory calculations which indicate a transition from direct dynamics at higher energies to a complex-mediated reaction under the present experimental conditions and point to an important role of intramolecular vibrational redistribution affecting the isotopic branching in this regime. The present results extend measurements into an astrochemically relevant energy regime and establish cryogenic single-ion chemistry as a new platform for resolving competing reaction pathways.
n0e2afbaeffd7: Photoemission is expected to occur when the photon energy exceeds the binding energy of an electron, with the photoemission yield generally remaining non-zero above this threshold. Yet, it can be suppressed at specific photon energies, a phenomenon known as the Cooper minimum. Although complete suppression represents an extreme limit of this phenomenon, such zero photoemission has previously been reported only for atoms with an outermost s-type orbital and has never been observed in non-atomic systems. Here, we demonstrate the deliberate realization of zero photoemission from Ag12W-, an artificial icosahedral superatom, by observing a vanishing photoemission cross section 0.85 eV above the detachment threshold and reproducing this behavior in theoretical simulations. These simulations predict that zero photoemission can be common in nearly spherical nanoclusters, a prediction we experimentally confirm using Ag12Mo-, an isoelectronic counterpart of Ag12W-. Because superatoms offer systematic control over both size and elemental composition using the periodic table, our findings establish a route toward active control of photoemission in finite-size quantum systems and stimulate further investigations of underexplored physical phenomena such as nondipole effects.
nd69a89a4048d: A sharp increase in gas uptake over a narrow pressure range can occur for fluids confined in nanoporous materials such as metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), reflecting a transformation between distinct adsorption states, often accompanied by the existence of metastable states. Understanding how co-adsorbed species modify this behavior is important for predicting and optimizing gas storage and separation. Here, we investigate the effect of CO2 on the adsorption transformation of confined CH4 in rigid IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8. Transition-Matrix Monte Carlo (TMMC) simulations were performed for systems containing 0-75 and 0-150 CO2 molecules in IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8, respectively. While the addition of CO2 decreases the maximum CH4 uptake, consistent with competition for pore space, remarkably, the presence of CO2 significantly shifts the discontinuity in the CH4 adsorption isotherm to substantially lower pressures relative to the pure CH4 system. This promotion of the high-density CH4 phase at lower pressures demonstrates that CO2 substantially alters the thermodynamic landscape governing confined CH4 through changes in both fluid-fluid and fluid-framework interactions. These results establish CO2 as a thermodynamic modifier of confined CH4 behavior and suggest that controlled co-adsorption provides a means of tuning adsorption transformations in nanoporous materials.
ne275fd95aa04: Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.
n87e22fcdd98c: Electrochemical etching (ECE) of n-type c-plane GaN enables the formation of porous architectures capable of enhancing the performance of optoelectronic devices and broadening the range of possible GaN applications. By varying the NaOH concentration within mixed electrolyte systems, the columnar pore shape, diameter, spacing, and bulk and surface porosity can be readily tuned. In addition to manually mixing NaOH with another etchant, aqueous basic electrolytes such as Na2CO3 and Na3PO4, each inherently containing significant hydroxide concentration through hydrolysis, also produce similar columnar pore morphologies, indicating that hydroxide plays the key role in directing the vertical pore growth. Chronoamperometry and pore structure analysis reveals that the mixed hydroxide-containing electrolyte systems exhibit a distinct, new ECE mechanism rather than a simple superposition of the individual ECE behaviour of each anion present. This work provides significant insight into the ECE mechanism for porous GaN, which is proposed to contain multiple reaction steps where hydroxide anions are involved in the formation of a reactive intermediate. These findings establish a versatile and controllable route for engineering columnar porous GaN architectures, offering significant advancement in applications requiring high porosity, ordered, and bespoke structures.
n4958b1eaa54e: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. IOB is preserved across nano- to microscale crystals and different double-perovskite compositions, broadly enabling information photonics and advanced sensing.
nc94402af299c: We report on the single-crystal growth, crystal structure, and physical properties of Yb$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$. Single crystal x-ray diffraction shows that the material crystallizes in the Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ structure-type at ambient conditions, described by orthorhombic symmetry $Pbam$. Magnetization measurements reveal a nearly isotropic diamagnetic response, indicating that Yb is stabilized in a non-magnetic divalent configuration. Electrical resistivity measurements show a metallic behavior. First-principles calculations including spin--orbit coupling describe a metal whose states at the Fermi level are dominated by Bi $6p$ orbitals, with a density of states within 1% of that of the isoelectronic compound Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$, consistent with a filled and chemically inert $4f$ shell. They further show that the nonsymmorphic symmetry of the crystal enforces fourfold-degenerate nodal lines on the Brillouin-zone boundary, four of which cross the Fermi level and give symmetry-enforced Dirac points with a linear transverse dispersion. Despite strong metallic and covalent bonding within the Pd-Bi network, Yb$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ is realized as a rare-earth analog of the Ca$_3$Pd$_4$Bi$_8$ structure type with divalent Yb ions. This result offers a potential avenue to discover other rare-earth analogs within this structural family.
n63d4e85983ed: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. Coherent electron pulses down to femtosecond durations reflect from the topmost atomic layers, imprinting the evolving surface profile onto their wavefronts. Defocus converts phase variations into image contrast. In a thin van der Waals material, we image the thermoelastic generation and propagation of picometre-amplitude acoustic waves. Measured dispersion relations, interpreted through elastodynamic modelling, distinguish substrate-supported and locally detached regions, revealing how interfacial contact shapes propagation. Delayed wave emission reveals scattering at buried mechanical defects. Our results establish electron-wavefront imaging of nanoscale surface dynamics, enabling the exploration of ultrafast energy transport, structural transformations and coupled mechanical, electronic and magnetic phenomena.
n56862991252b: Many functionally important materials, such as silicon, possess high-symmetry crystal structures that forbid even-order nonlinear optical responses, thereby limiting their application in e.g., photonics and optoelectronics. Strain gradients can effectively break symmetries, activating otherwise forbidden optical responses. Although such flexo-photoresponses have attracted considerable interest recently, a comprehensive microscopic theoretical framework is still lacking. Here, we develop a first-principles approach that can systematically evaluate a wide range of flexo-photoresponses in realistic materials. By mapping strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons within the established theory of electron-phonon coupling, our approach captures the nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects of lattice deformations on nonlinear optical responses. Applying the framework to prototypical centrosymmetric materials, including Si, cubic $\rm SrTiO_3$, and monolayer black phosphorus, we demonstrate that a strain gradients of $10^5\sim10^6~\rm m^{-1}$ can induce flexo-second-harmonic generation and flexo-bulk photovoltaic effects comparable to the intrinsic responses of non-centrosymmetric crystals. Our work establishes a rigorous foundation for strain gradient engineering of light-matter interactions, opening new avenues for nanoscale optomechanics, optoelectronics, and beyond.
na33281bf9cfe: Optically addressable paramagnetic defects in silicon carbide (SiC) are attractive for scalable quantum technologies such as quantum sensing. PL5, PL6, and PL7 are promising defects for their high brightness and spin-readout contrast. Although generation by oxygen implantation has been reported very recently, nonuniform spin and optical properties and the limited generation depth of implanted defects hinder both high-sensitivity sensing and conclusive microscopic identification. Here we engineer high-quality defects by decoupling oxygen incorporation and defect formation, realizing highly homogeneous spin-resonance frequencies as well as narrow optical linewidths and long T2* coherence time. Further, we demonstrate defect formation beyond the ion range utilizing oxygen diffusion, exceptional among impurities in SiC. We further provide hyperfine-interaction statistics of 17O and host nuclei across many PL6 defects, making the oxygen-vacancy origin conclusive. Together, the microscopic identification and the demonstrated formation route establish a foundation for developing the oxygen-vacancy spin defect into a versatile quantum platform.
n7bb3158c1a07: Crystal symmetry governs the physical properties of materials and provides the framework for interpreting their microscopic excitations and macroscopic responses. In altermagnets, the crystal symmetries that relate opposite-spin sublattices give rise to momentum-dependent spin splitting despite compensated magnetization. Determining the real crystal symmetry is therefore essential for understanding the intrinsic electronic and magnetic properties. For the altermagnetic semiconductor $α$-MnTe, conflicting Raman assignments have left both its intrinsic lattice excitations and its crystal symmetry unresolved. Here we combine high-resolution Raman and second-harmonic generation (SHG) spectroscopy with first-principles calculations to distinguish intrinsic lattice excitations from Te-derived spectral contributions and to examine bulk inversion symmetry of $α$-MnTe. We show that several prominent Raman features previously assigned to $α$-MnTe instead originate from segregated Te clusters or precipitates. The remaining intrinsic Raman response consists of a single Raman-active mode assigned to the calculated $E_{2g}$ phonon, consistent with the centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ symmetry. The SHG response agrees with surface electric-dipole and bulk electric-quadrupole contributions expected for a centrosymmetric $D_{6h}$ crystal, supporting the preservation of bulk inversion symmetry in $α$-MnTe. Our findings revise the Raman assignments in $α$-MnTe and provide a basis for interpreting its altermagnetic properties within the appropriate crystal-symmetry framework.
n36622cab1893: NbN thin films with a nominal thickness of 10 nm were grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) on Al$_2$O$_3$-buffered Si substrates and treated with oxygen plasma for 0 s (untreated), 20 s, 40 s, and 60 s to investigate oxygen-induced changes in their optical properties. Spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) measurements were performed before and after oxygen plasma treatment over the ultraviolet-visible-near-infrared (1.24-6.20 eV) and infrared (0.041-0.827 eV) spectral ranges. Film thickness determined by X-ray reflectivity (XRR) was used as a fixed parameter in the optical modeling to extract the dielectric function, optical constants, and effective free-carrier concentration. We observed the emergence of a distinct absorption feature near 4.9 eV following oxygen plasma treatment, consistent with the oxidation of the NbN surface and the resulting change in its optical properties. Increasing the treatment time from 0 to 60 s reduced the effective carrier concentration from $1.20 \times 10^{22}$ to $1.03 \times 10^{22}$ cm$^{-3}$ and the effective carrier mobility from 2.44 to 2.27 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. The obtained results provide a basis for understanding the effects of oxygen plasma treatment on NbN thin films.
n82ec59c6d244: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms underlying polyamorphic transitions requires simultaneous knowledge of thermodynamic and structural evolution, which has remained experimentally inaccessible. Here, we combine chip-based fast differential scanning calorimetry with high-energy synchrotron X-ray diffraction to simultaneously probe the thermodynamic and structural evolution during the polyamorphic transition of a Pd-Ni-P metallic glass. Correlating heat-flow signals with the corresponding structural evolution during both heating and cooling reveals a direct relationship between thermodynamic evolution and medium-range structural ordering. Based on this relationship, we identify two distinct transition mechanisms. In the glassy state, the transition proceeds continuously through progressive medium-range ordering, accompanied by enhanced thermal stability and strongly temperature-dependent kinetics. In contrast, in the equilibrium supercooled liquid, the transition proceeds through the coexistence of distinct amorphous states, with only a weak temperature dependence of the kinetics. These findings show that atomic mobility governs the transformation pathway by coupling thermodynamic evolution to structural ordering, providing new insights into polyamorphic transitions in nonequilibrium amorphous systems.
n2cabcf9c6a98: Removing one chalcogen layer from a transition-metal dichalcogenide monolayer leaves an undercoordinated sheet that reconstructs as the remaining chalcogen atoms cross the metal plane. Here, we combine \textit{ab initio} and reactive molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of depleted MoS$_2$, MoSe$_2$, and Janus MoSSe, examining each remaining chalcogen on two parent lattices, to show that the remaining chalcogen type determines the structural reconstruction, with only a minor influence from the parent lattice. In \textit{ab initio} trajectories of the Janus-derived sheets, Se crosses the Mo plane already at 300~K, whereas S stays in place at 300~K and the sheet reconstructs only at 900~K. With a free in-plane cell, the crossings precede an anisotropic lattice contraction, which therefore results from the structural reconstruction. Reactive MD simulations of 50~nm sheets show that, when S remains, the Mo lattice stays crystalline in nanometric domains that disappear with time and temperature, with pores/holes at 900~K. In contrast, when Se remains, the Mo lattice loses crystalline order within the first picosecond, and 36--39\% of the Se atoms cross at every temperature. In a depleted lateral MoS$_2$/MoSe$_2$ heterostructure, both modes coexist in one sheet, each half reconstructing like its single-chalcogen counterpart, suggesting chalcogen patterning as a route to define crystalline and disordered regions in a single monolayer.
n430be191f31a: Crystal materials are designed either by screening known crystals for a target property or by generating new crystals with that property. Both routes are judged against public databases of known crystals, but these databases name the same crystal differently. Several materials announced as new by recent generative and autonomous discovery campaigns have since proved to be known phases or close variants of them. The limits of both routes remain unmeasured. Here we probe them by matching the crystals of 55 databases by structure into one self-extending database of 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values, each traced to its source. Only 4.5% of its crystal-property pairs carry a value. To fill the empty pairs, we developed CGTNet, an equivariant graph transformer with state-of-the-art accuracy on several tasks of two public benchmarks. Trained on each task, it forms a library of property models whose predictions we release. The reach of forward screening has been underestimated. Known crystals hold tens of thousands of ultra-incompressible candidates without a recorded bulk modulus, and a post hoc audit of synthesis evidence finds among them ReN2, whose bulk modulus was measured at 428 GPa. The novelty claimed for inverse design has been overestimated. At an equal verification budget, a stiffness-conditioned generator returned more stiff hits than screening (100 versus 55), but all contained osmium and 82 repeated recorded compositions. Integrating and completing the databases of known crystals therefore moves the limits of both routes: it widens what screening can reach and sets the reference against which generated crystals are judged new.
n4aaf655f5229: Organic molecules are versatile building blocks for the formation of complex low-dimensional nanostructures on surfaces. Recently, interest has grown in translating on-surface synthetic protocols from noble metal surfaces to insulating surfaces, which offer technological relevance, and to magnetic or superconducting surfaces, which offer new routes to correlated phases. It is important, therefore, to understand how these alternative surfaces may alter the properties of adsorbates through processes like charge transfer and screening. Evidence for charge transfer is often obtained experimentally via scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) and spectroscopy (STS), and theoretically via density functional theory (DFT). In this work, we systematically compare the properties of isolated macrocyclic emeraldine (Me$_6$) molecules on three different surfaces: metallic Au(111), a semiconducting ferromagnetic monolayer of FeCl$_2$, and a cleaved superconducting surface of bulk 2H-NbSe$_2$. We show that STS and DFT alone are insufficient to quantify charge transfer for these cases. Instead, we complement these methods with Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) measurements and model Hamiltonian calculations to demonstrate that on Au(111) and FeCl$_2$, Me$_6$ molecules donate a single electron to the substrate, whereas on NbSe$_2$ two electrons are transferred from molecule to substrate. Our work provides insight into the interplay of charge transfer, screening, and molecule-substrate coupling, and develops experimental and theoretical methods for comparing the properties of adsorbates across different surfaces for future studies.
n1db878ecc69a: High-efficiency vertical charge transport in multilayer organic optoelectronic devices highly depends on molecular structure and arrangement. Using two T2-(NDI-T2)2 conjugated oligomers with ethylhexyl (EH) and octyldodecyl (OD) side chains as a model system, their effects on electron transport are investigated using, among other techniques, atomic force microscopy (AFM), conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM), grazing-incidence wide-angle X-ray scattering (GIWAXS), steady-state optical spectroscopy, and time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations. The oligomers of both materials exhibit relatively disordered structures in the as-cast state, whereas annealing enhances structural order and leads to side-chain-dependent changes in molecular stacking. EH-based films show a smaller annealing-induced photoluminescence shift than OD-based films, suggesting less pronounced stacking and conformational rearrangements, consistent with TDDFT-supported exciton analysis. The current-voltage characteristics are analyzed using the space-charge-limited current (SCLC) model. After annealing, both materials exhibit improved vertical electron mobility. The EH-based films reach a maximum mobility of 1.2 x 10^-4 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1. The combined results suggest that the shorter EH side chains modify the out-of-plane packing environment and facilitate vertical electron transport. These results establish a structure-property relationship between side-chain structure, molecular order, exciton coupling and vertical mobility, providing a molecular design basis for optimising organic semiconductors through side-chain engineering.
ne33041cd0936: Sluggish vacancy-mediated self-diffusion in lithium metal limits the critical current density (CCD) of Li anodes in solid-state batteries by promoting interfacial void formation during stripping. Using an adaptation of the Lomer model for the dilute limit, we show that only Ag, Ge, and Cd solid solutions are predicted to reach $1~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ within their solubility limits. The thermodynamically estimated CCD of Ag at $\sim 9$ at.% reaches $\sim 4~\mathrm{mA~cm^{-2}}$ at a theoretical capacity of $1522~\mathrm{mAh~g^{-1}}$. Migration barrier calculations indicate that the enhancement may be partially offset by vacancy trapping, necessitating further validation via molecular dynamics simulations. Notably, Hume-Rothery rules alone prove insufficient as prefilters, whereas machine-learning models trained on the DFT data can eliminate most unsuitable solutes early in the funnel and extend the workflow to related solid-solution searches.
nf0932858f68f: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. The residual magnetic field is actively minimized to below 400 pT through a combination of mu-metal magnetic shielding and internal compensation coils. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. These results demonstrate that high-buffer-pressure single-beam OPMs can achieve excellent sensitivity, establishing a pathway toward compact and scalable arrays.
nda48ba1d4694: Very recently, Mahanti et al. (arXiv:2609.18735) introduced the observational ergotropic advantage, which gives the maximum value of extra work that a measurement can obtain with respect to all incoherent measurements. However, the above quantity does not show monotonic behaviour under the resource theory of measurement coherence. So, the search for a resource theory in which it is a monotone was open. We derive the monotonicity of this quantity using energy-preserving channels and passive resets as free operations and energy-incoherent measurements as free objects. We show the monotonicity property of the measure as a necessary criterion of measurement transformation, but it turns out not to be a sufficient condition. It is further established that the measure is not convex. A short analysis of bounds and tightness of the measure using a degenerate Hamiltonian is also given.
n8ac410cb9d49: In this paper, we present various well-studied examples of quantum systems, and discuss how they might be analysed algebraically. We analyse the harmonic oscillator, hydrogenic atom, optical components, and particle spin using multiple algebraic methods, and highlight the central importance of algebraic relationships between operators in determining the physical character of the system. In particular, we show: the ubiquity of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{so}(2,1)\cong\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ as the ``spectrum generating algebra''; the role of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and $\mathfrak{su}(1,1)$ in determining the action of optical components; that an elementary algebraic approach to particle spin offers novel insights into its nature versus the usual approaches; and how understanding the full (often hidden) symmetry of a problem enables it to be solved immediately without the need to solve differential equations. We hope this work will serve as a gentle introduction to algebraic methods in quantum mechanics for the interested reader --- we therefore signpost active areas of research within the community.
n98a40ece9c89: Information causality is a physical principle that constrains bipartite post-quantum nonlocal correlations from information-theoretic assumptions. A direct characterization of the correlations satisfying it, however, remains difficult because the defining entropic condition must hold for all admissible protocols in the corresponding task. Here, we formulate the single-copy information causality problem as an optimization over all protocol parameters and simplify it by proving a deterministic reduction. We then show that generic adaptive multi-copy protocols can be represented as single-copy protocols applied to an effective behavior obtained by local wirings. As a consequence, for families of correlations closed under wirings, excluding single-copy violations suffices to exclude all finite-copy adaptive-protocol violations. We formulate the resulting membership and set-inclusion problems as optimization problems and discuss possible semidefinite programming relaxations. As an application, we study expansions of the information causality functional around zero-capacity channels, generalizing a method recently employed by Gachechiladze and Miklin to derive the Tsirelson--Landau--Masanes boundary from information causality. For expansions centered on channels whose output distribution has full support, imposing the second-order constraints for all single-copy protocols characterizes exactly the set of macroscopic locality in the CHSH scenario. Expanding instead around appropriate constant-output channels with perturbations that change the channel support, we show that every single-copy IC violation can be witnessed already at first order with a channel of arbitrarily small capacity.
n63669c90101a: Model-independent tests of quantum theory, such as Bell inequality violations, focus on static properties of the theory and do not rely on its dynamical aspects. Hence, this core part of quantum theory remains largely untested in a model-independent way. We show that the structure of quantum time evolution can be examined by testing the consistency between the state space and the dynamical laws. Considering a class of generalized phase-space theories, we find that certain quantum states can only be part of a theory if the time evolution is quantum: their evolution in anharmonic potentials would otherwise result in unphysical, negative marginal distributions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the existence of the first excited state of a quantum harmonic oscillator is already sufficient to single out the Moyal bracket (quantum dynamics) to leading order in $\hbar^2$. We outline how theory-independent Wigner tomography of this state can be used to empirically exclude nonquantum dynamical theories.
n48ddc86e838e: Scaling parametrized quantum circuits to a larger number of qubits is a central challenge in Quantum Machine Learning: gradient estimation via the parameter-shift rule quickly becomes prohibitively expensive, while gradient-free optimizers offer limited convergence guarantees. We apply the Pauli propagation framework to a broad class of Quantum Machine Learning problems in which the loss is expressed as a function of expectation values of the circuit's observables, while keeping the relevant quantity of interest, such as the quantum state or its samples, classically intractable to compute. By propagating the observables backward through the circuit, we obtain an explicit parametric expression for the loss that can be minimized entirely on classical hardware. We also present complementary strategies to make propagation tractable at large scale, including weight-based and degree-based truncations and pruning heuristics. We demonstrate the approach on two benchmarks run on 64-qubit circuits: Variational Quantum Eigensolver on a two-dimensional Ising model, and training of a discrete-type generative model for binary images. In both cases, the classically pre-trained parameters are deployed on the IBM quantum processor ibm_berlin. For generative learning, we additionally show that the circuits considered here require substantially fewer parametrized gates than IQP-style ansätze, reducing transpilation overhead and making deployment on current quantum hardware feasible.
nef7102679b9d: The fidelity of direct numerical simulation now outpaces the storage and data-movement capacity available for the resulting fields. We present an open, distributed, GPU-accelerated low-rank compression framework for large turbulent flow databases. We assess it using two direct numerical simulations of a controlled diffusion compressor cascade under laminar and turbulent inflow conditions. Compression is formulated using a correlation operator over space and time, which is two orders of magnitude larger than that of snapshot POD. Its dominant range is extracted with a randomized range finder based on communication-avoiding hierarchical QR. The compressed databases are evaluated through a hierarchy of increasingly strict diagnostics, from instantaneous reconstruction and second-order statistics to the modal turbulent kinetic energy budget and its nonlinear interscale transfer. The budget terms are far more sensitive to compression than fieldwise or one-point errors. They remain accurate at conservative compression and degrade sharply once the retained energy is relaxed. The near-wall dissipation and the interscale transfer degrade the most and set the admissible compression level. An aggressive reduction preserves every one-point statistic to within a few per cent while corrupting both by an order of magnitude more. The dissipation error is confined to the viscous sublayer and grows with the development of the boundary layer. It is carried by the high-order modes. For both inflows, the linear budget terms scale with the discarded energy to the power $0.8$ and the triadic transfer to a power above one.
nf16b0b2ec77a: Cameras in the surf zone or behind ship wakes look through turbid, bubbly, moving water close to the lens, yet restoration networks are usually scored only on displayed images. We introduce a measured dataset of a telescope viewing displayed images and physical objects through a 25~mm water layer 45~mm in front of its objective, under seven combinations of flow, bubbles and turbidity, with clear-water recordings as a second reference.
